segments.he: עיין ליקוטי הלכות הלכות דברים הנוהגים בסעודה הלכה ד' מבואר שם כל ענין ר"ה יו"כ סוכות והד' מינים ע"פ מאמר זה עיין שם:
segments.en:
And in Likutay Mohara"n, Siman 1, in the discourse Tik'u Mimshola
["Blow the Shofar of Sovereignty"], it is explained regarding the great Tzadikim,
who are in the dimension (bechia) of being the Place of the World
— and they are able to perform the [spiritual work of] Rosh HaShanah.
And in the discourse Tik'u Emuna, Siman 5,
much is explained regarding the wondrous rectifications
that are wrought through the gathering of the disciples near the true Rebbe —
and the primary time of gathering is on Rosh HaShanah.

In Siman 40, Mi SheYodeia M'Eretz Yisroel
["One Who Knows from Eretz Yisroel"], it is explained likewise
that the primary great gathering near the Tzadik is on Rosh HaShanah,
and one who merits to be near a true Tzadik on Rosh HaShanah —
in every place that this person gazes,
the air there becomes of the dimension of the air of Eretz Yisroel.

And more is explained in many discourses in his holy books
regarding the holiness of Rosh HaShanah, the soundings of the Shofar,
and the general holiness of the month of Tishray.
See also Likutay Mohara"n, Siman 94,
which likewise explains that one must travel to Tzadikim on Rosh HaShanah.

But beyond what is written, he spoke about this many times orally,
as is explained somewhat in his holy conversations.
He said explicitly that
"all his purpose and all his concern is Rosh HaShanah",
and he declared: "My Rosh HaShanah surpasses everything."
He admonished all those close to him that they should all be with him on Rosh HaShanah —
not one absent —
for "all my affair is only Rosh HaShanah," etc.

And once he said:
"With me, the main thing is Rosh HaShanah" — and also:
"My Rosh HaShanah is a great novelty (chidush) …
not only are you all certainly bound to my Rosh HaShanah,
but even all the world — the entire world — depends upon my Rosh HaShanah."

On the last Erev Rosh HaShanah of his holy life,
he spoke very much about this —
about the great obligation and necessity for all those close to him
to be with him on Rosh HaShanah.
He answered and said in a strong voice, from the depths of his heart:
"What shall I tell you? There is nothing greater than this"
— meaning, to be with him on Rosh HaShanah.

And once he said that on Rosh HaShanah he performs matters and rectifications
— even for the souls of those close to him who come to him on Rosh HaShanah —
that throughout the entire year, even he himself cannot perform them.

From the import of his words — and especially from what he spoke so much about on the last Erev Rosh HaShanah,
as mentioned — his holy disciples, z"l, understood that
his firm will was that all those close to him should gather to him on Rosh HaShanah
even after his passing —
that is, to pray at his grave on Erev Rosh HaShanah,
as is explained in the Shulchan Aruch that it is the custom to go and pray at the graves of Tzadikim
on Erev Rosh HaShanah.
And also on Rosh HaShanah itself, all his holy gathering would pray together in connection with him, z"l,
and with all the Tzadikim of the generation
— those who dwell in the dust —
and thereby wondrous rectifications would be accomplished,
just as during his physical lifetime.

His disciples, z"l, accepted this upon themselves and agreed to do so every Rosh HaShanah.
And with G-d's help, this has already been [the practice] for more than sixty years*
after his passing, z"l —
and even so, the matter continues among the Anash [Breslov Chassidim]
for generations eternal, as is well known.

The asterisk (*) refers to the time of original composition of this work, over sixty years after Rebbe Nachman's passing in 5571 (1810 CE). Rabbi Nachman of Tchehrin composed this work in the later 19th century.

Now, on this Rosh HaShanah,
it occurred to me:
since our Rebbe, z"l, declared explicitly and with full voice
that all his purpose and all his concern is Rosh HaShanah —
and since this is the general principle stated above —
it is understood on its own
that in all of his holy discourses,
even those not delivered on Rosh HaShanah
and in which Rosh HaShanah is not mentioned at all —
nonetheless, the topic of Rosh HaShanah is certainly hidden and clothed within them as well.

Therefore I set my heart to examine his discourses, z"l,
and to search within them —
perhaps I would find some allusions (rmazim) to the topic of Rosh HaShanah in each of his discourses.
And with G-d's help, I found some allusions in most of his discourses, z"l, to the topic of Rosh HaShanah.

It is well known, as is explained in holy books,
regarding the holiness of Rosh HaShanah —
that it encompasses the holiness of the entire year.
Just as one merits to receive the holiness of Rosh HaShanah,
so one merits to conduct oneself in the holiness of one's service to G-d
throughout the entire year.
And in particular, all the holiness of the festive times of the month of Tishray —
such as the holiness of Yom Kippur, Sukkos,
and all the holiness of the mitzvos observed during them
until after Sh'mini Atzeres —
is certainly all included within the holiness of Rosh HaShanah.

As is understood in the holy Zohar and in the intentions (kavanos) of the Ar"i z"l:
all the rectifications that are accomplished from Rosh HaShanah
until after Sh'mini Atzeres are all bound and interwoven with one another.
Because of this, I have mostly alluded within them also to the topic of Yom Kippur, Sukkos, and Sh'mini Atzeres.

Because I knew the great weight of the smallness of my poor understanding —
even though I am firm in my view that certainly in each of his discourses, z"l,
there is the topic of Rosh HaShanah as mentioned above —
still, I knew that if my understanding were broader,
one could certainly explain within this many wonders from the words of our Rabbis, z"l,
in the hidden and revealed Torah.
For the thoughts of our holy Rebbe, z"l, are very deep and exalted,
and wonders of wisdom are hidden within his discourses.

Because of the great smallness of my understanding,
I am far from grasping this —
and would that I merit to understand at least the plain meaning of his holy words, z"l.
Therefore I have abbreviated in all these matters as much as possible,
and have come here only to mention and to arouse the heart of the reader
to search through each of his discourses, z"l,
regarding the holiness of Rosh HaShanah, etc. —
and certainly one whose understanding is truly broad,
who sets his mind and heart to these matters,
will find therein many wonders.
And this shall be my reward —
that I have begun to walk on this path —
even if it is not in my power to complete the matter as is fitting.

The Sages, z"l, have already said:
"All words of Torah are good"
— and when one merits to hit upon the truth even in one matter of Torah,
it is certainly more precious than all wealth,
and gold and silver cannot be compared to it.

Because of all the above:
in places where I knew that the topic of Rosh HaShanah as understood through a given discourse
is already explained in Likutay Halachos,
I noted only to look there — and I did not see fit to explain it further,
fulfilling the verse: "And in the place of the great — do not stand"
[Prov. 25:6].
All the more so in discourses where our Rebbe, z"l, himself explained
that this is the topic of Rosh HaShanah —
I certainly feared to touch them,
for "What has straw to do with grain?"
[Jer. 23:28]
and one does not mix the mundane with the holy of holies.

Also, the reader should know:
all these matters were written mostly in great brevity and in the manner of mere chapter-headings.
Because of this, in many places it will appear to the reader at first glance
that the matters are not explained and ordered as is proper.
But when one sets one's heart to study them with a truthful eye —
I trust in the Almighty that one will find in them a taste,
and the eyes of one's understanding will open
to find many precious virtues (segulahs)
hinted at in the words of our Rabbis, z"l, in these matters.
And this would be my reward.

I called this small volume
Yerech HaAisonim — "The Month of the Mighty Ones" —
after the verse:
"In the month of Eisanim (Mighty Ones), at the Festival — that is the seventh month"
[I Kings 8:2].
And our Sages, z"l, expounded:
"The month that the mighty ones [= the Patriarchs] were born in it" —
and this is the foundation of the entire volume:
the month of Tishray with all its festivals and holy mitzvos that are observed in it.

May G-d place our portion in His Torah,
and may He place in our hearts love for Him and fear of Him,
to do His will and to serve Him with a whole heart. Amen, so may it be His will.

It is possible that the author called this holy book Yerech HaAisonim
[spelled as in the verse in Kings 8 — האיתנים] —
because the verse as written: "Yerech HaAisanim"
[ירח האתנים — without the yud] —
together with the [standard] total (im haKolel) —
equals in gematria [numerology] the name
Nachman ben HaRav Tzvi Aryeh —
to allude to his name in the naming of the book,
as the early authorities, z"l, wrote [it was customary to do].

Siman 1 — Ashray Smimay Dorech [Ps. 119:1 — "Fortunate are those of perfect way"]

Theme: Rosh HaShanah

Rosh HaShanah is for the Sun; Rosh Chodesh is for the Moon

Rosh HaShanah corresponds to the sun,
and Rosh Chodesh [the New Month] corresponds to the moon
— these being the dimensions (bechinahs) of the letters
חי״ת (Ches) and נו״ן (Nun).

Key Kabbalistic Correspondences in This Section:

Ches [ח] — Chochma (Wisdom); the Sun; the masculine-giving principle.

Nun [נ] — Malchus (Sovereignty/Kingdom); the Moon; the feminine-receiving principle.

Malchus d'Kedusha — the Kingdom of Holiness.

Malchus d'Stra Achra — the Kingdom of the Other Side [the forces of evil].

Because the Nun is the dimension of Malchus (Sovereignty)
— which has nothing of its own and receives only from the Ches,
which is the dimension of the Sun, etc. —
therefore Rosh Chodesh is not mentioned on Rosh HaShanah.
And the Sages, z"l, said:
"One remembrance [in the Musaf prayer] serves for both"
[Rosh HaShanah 30b].

Therefore one prays greatly at that time
for his children — the holy Malchus and the Kingdom of the Messiah —
and also for the revelation of the holy Daas (Knowledge/Consciousness),
"and all that is formed shall know that You have formed it",
and for the nullification of the kingdom of the Stra Achra
— the dimension of "for You shall remove the dominion of wickedness from the earth".

This is the dimension of HaMelech HaKadosh — "The Holy King" —
which is declared during [the Rosh HaShanah and Ten Days of Repentance prayers]:
the dimension of the connection of Malchus — the dimension of Nun —
with the Ches, which is the dimension of Wisdom, the dimension of Holiness.

This is the dimension of "Remember us for life, O King Who desires life"
— for "Wisdom gives life"
[Eccl. 7:12].
And the holy Malchus is also the dimension of life,
the dimension of "David, King of Israel, is alive and enduring"
[Rosh HaShanah 25a].
And it is written: "In the light of the King's countenance is life"
[Prov. 16:15].

Therefore We Travel to Tzadikim on Rosh HaShanah

Therefore we travel to Tzadikim on Rosh HaShanah,
for the Tzadik is the one who is fully engaged in this:
to give strength to the holy Malchus
— which is the dimension of the good inclination (Yetzer Tov) —
to overcome the Malchus d'Stra Achra — the evil inclination (Yetzer Hora);
and to draw down to the Malchus a complete illumination from the Supernal Wisdom,
and to bind her to it.

The Tzadik is Called "The Book of Life"

Therefore the Tzadik is called "Sefer HaChaim" — "The Book of Life"
— as brought in the Tikunim;
and also Malchus is called "Sefer HaChaim",
as brought in the Kavanos [Kabbalistic meditations].
That is: through the Tzadik,
the supernal life is drawn down from its root to [the Malchus].

This is the dimension of the shape of the letter Tzadik
[צ] —
which is composed of Yud-Nun, as is brought:
the dimension of the union of Wisdom — the dimension of Yud —
as is known — with Malchus, the dimension of Nun.

This is the dimension of the matter of Esov and Yaakov
that takes place on Rosh HaShanah,
as brought in the holy Zohar —
for Yaakov binds himself at all times to the Supernal Wisdom,
and therefore merited the birthright,
as is explained in the main text;
and Esov is the opposite of this —
the dimension of "for he had [Esov's] game in his mouth"
[Gen. 25:28]
— [meaning,] he clothes himself in mitzvos [outwardly, without inner truth].

Therefore We Pray Greatly for Awe [on Rosh HaShanah]

Therefore we pray greatly for Yirah (awe/fear [of G-d]) at that time —
for Yirah is from the dimension of the awe that is of Malchus, as is known;
and it is the very essence of Wisdom, as it is stated:
"Behold, the fear of G-d — that is Wisdom"
[Job 28:28],
and it is written: "The beginning of Wisdom is the fear of G-d"
[Ps. 111:10].

This is the dimension of Malchuyos, Zichronos, and Shofaros
[the three blessings of the Rosh HaShanah Musaf prayer]:
Malchuyos — corresponding to the dimension of Malchus;
Zichronos — corresponding to the dimension of connecting to the intellect (sechel)
present in all things
— the dimension of "fortunate is the man who will not forget You",
and how G-d, as it were, turns His heart to all the creatures of the world,
knowing all their affairs — all their deeds, speech, and thought;
and He examines the works of them all.
From this it is understood how a person must be constantly connected and cleaved to G-d,
and gaze only upon the sechel (intellect/inner wisdom) in every thing,
in order to draw near to G-d through that very thing.

As is brought in the Kavanos: Zichronos correspond to Chochma-Bina-Daas
[Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge] — the secret of the intellects
wherein lies the secret of remembrance.

Shofaros — the blessing of Ata Niglaysa ["You were revealed"],
which speaks of the topic of the Giving of the Torah —
corresponds to the dimension of the Torah,
through which strength is given to the holy Malchus
to overpower the Malchus d'Stra Achra.
For the Torah emerges from Wisdom and Understanding,
and there is the secret of the source of the Great Supernal Shofar —
through which all the scattered of Israel will be gathered
and the dimension of the Malchus d'Stra Achra will be nullified.
And this is the dimension of the Shofar of Rosh HaShanah —
for it is the first day of the Ten Days of Repentance (Aseres Y'may Tshuva),
and one must humble the evil inclination (Yetzer HaRa)
— the dimension of the Malchus d'Stra Achra —
and give strength to the holy Malchus.
And this is accomplished through the Shofar.

Afterwards One Engages in Repentance Through the Ten Days

Afterwards one engages in repentance throughout all the Ten Days of Repentance,
until one merits on Yom Kippur
— when "the Mother and the Daughter ascend together"
[Zohar] —
meaning, Malchus receives vitality from the Supernal Wisdom through Bina (Understanding), the Supernal Mother.
Then the evil inclination is completely subdued,
until "the Accuser has no authority to prosecute"
[Yoma 20a],
and then the light of the moon becomes like the light of the sun.
Therefore one sanctifies the new moon on the night after Yom Kippur.

And this is the dimension of the prayers of Yom Kippur —
for through the above, all prayers and requests are accepted.
This is the dimension of the Three Books that are opened on Rosh HaShanah:
complete Tzadikim — who cleave themselves always to the sechel and Wisdom
wherein lies the essence of life —
are therefore immediately inscribed for life;
complete wicked people — who cleave to the spirit of folly of the evil inclination
and are distant from the holy Wisdom —
are therefore immediately inscribed for death,
the dimension of "they die, and not in wisdom"
[Job 4:21];
and the intermediate ones are suspended until Yom Kippur, as mentioned above.

After Yom Kippur — Sukkos

After Yom Kippur one enters the Sukka.
The Torah said: "Leave your permanent dwelling and dwell in a temporary dwelling"
— meaning, a person should not make the world of this life a permanent dwelling,
but only a temporary dwelling;
and his primary permanence shall be in the intellect (sechel) and the inner dimension
present in every thing.
For "wherever a person directs his thought — there is the person's whole being"
[as brought in Chassidic writings].
Therefore the primary permanence of one's thought shall be in the sechel of every thing,
which is the dimension of the World to Come,
"and the earth shall be filled with knowledge [of G-d]"
[Is. 11:9]
— this is the portion of Yaakov,
who took the World to Come for himself.
Even though he too must necessarily pass through this world,
it is only in the manner of a temporary dwelling.

The Light of the Intellect and the Sukka's Shade

Because the light of the sechel — which is the dimension of the sun — is exceedingly great,
and it is impossible to merit it except through the dimension of Nun,
the dimension of Malchus, the dimension of contraction (tzimtzum),
therefore one must be in a Sukka
whose shade exceeds its light
(tzilosoh m'ruba m'chamsah).

And therefore a Sukka that is more than twenty cubits high is invalid —
because "the eye cannot govern it"
[the eye cannot see into it properly] —
for the essential [purpose] is to gaze with an open eye
at the sechel present in every thing.
This is the dimension of the Sukka which is
"a reminder of the Clouds of Glory"
— about which it is said:
"which eye has not seen — You, G-d, and Your cloud stands over them"
[Is. 64:3].

And likewise if it is less than ten handbreadths [from the ground], it is invalid —
for "the Divine Presence never descended below ten [handbreadths]"
[Sukkah 5a].
And there is where the primary foothold of Esov — the domain of the husks (klippos) — lies.
Therefore if the s'chach [roofing] is lower than ten handbreadths,
it is the dimension of drawing Wisdom down into the domain of the husks, heaven forbid —
the dimension of "they are wise — to do evil"
[Jer. 4:22] —
and it is therefore called a "putrid dwelling",
the dimension of "their Wisdom became putrid."
For the essence of Wisdom and intellect is to gaze upward — above ten [handbreadths] —
above all the vanities of this world.

And therefore it is required that stars be visible through the s'chach,
and the legal authorities have explained that this means
the radiance of the sun is meant [i.e., gaps through which sunlight can pass]
[see Beis Yosef],
for the sechel is the dimension of the light of the sun.

The Four Species of the Lulav

This is the dimension of the mitzvah of taking the
four species of the lulav —
they correspond to the four letters of the holy Name Havaya
[the Tetragrammaton],
and they correspond to the Patriarchs, and the Matriarchs,
and to all the general groupings within Israel,
as the Sages, z"l, expounded.

One waves them upward and downward and in all four directions of the world —
to declare and reveal and publicize in the world
that all the world and its fullness, and all that is in it,
contains a great inner dimension (p'nimius),
the dimension of "the earth is full of Your acquisitions"
[Ps. 104:24]
— and the primary acquisition is Wisdom and Knowledge (Daas) of holiness,
the dimension of "with knowledge you have acquired"
and the dimension of "this one acquired Wisdom"
— for in every thing in the world there is intellect and wisdom,
and one must gaze only upon the sechel in every thing
in order to draw near to G-d through it,
as one perceives concretely in these four species —
that wondrous sublime matters are hinted within their inner dimension.

See the Zohar, Vayechi, p. 220b,
where it expounds the verse "All who are called by My Name"
[Is. 43:7] regarding the four species —
and it is somewhat aligned with our topic.
And the Midrash Rabba, Parshas Emor, states that Shlomo [King Solomon] said
of this: "And four which I did not know"
[Prov. 30:18] — these are the four species of the lulav —
and concludes regarding them: "And they are wise, they are made wise"
— meaning, a wonderful Wisdom is clothed within them.
Therefore they grow over [all kinds of] water —
for the essential means to merit this is through the Torah, which is called water.
And therefore the Sages, z"l, said:
"They hint that we have been victorious in the war [begun] on Rosh HaShanah"
— meaning, the war between Yaakov and Esov described above.

On Account of This the Sages Said…

And therefore the Sages, z"l, said:
"Say before Me Malchuyos on Rosh HaShanah
— so that you will crown Me over you;
Zichronos — so that your remembrance will rise before Me for good;
and through what? Through the Shofar."
[Rosh HaShanah 16a]

In merit of taking the four species on the first day [of Sukkos],
"I will reveal Myself to you as the First"
[i.e., the Blessed One will be first to benefit you]
— meaning, one merits the revelation of His G-dliness and drawing near to Him
through the intellect found in every thing.
This is "the First" — the dimension of "the beginning is Wisdom"
[Reishis Chochma],
and the Targum renders Bereishis [In the Beginning] as B'Chochma [With Wisdom].
"And He pays back to you from the First — this is the wicked Esov"
— meaning one subdues the husk (klippa) of Esov which is the opposite of this, as above.
"And He builds for you the First — this is the Temple"
— wherein is the primary revelation of His G-dliness and holy Knowledge.
And therefore: "Whoever possesses knowledge, it is as though the Temple was built in his days"
[Berachos 33a].
"And He brings for you the First — this is King Messiah"
— meaning the dimension of Malchus, the dimension of Nun, mentioned above,
of which it is said concerning King Messiah:
"Before the sun, Yinon is His name"
[Ps. 72:17],
as the Sages, z"l, expounded.

One can allude all four of these matters in the mitzvah of the four species themselves —
but this is not the place [to elaborate upon it].

Afterwards One Merits Sh'mini Atzeres

Afterwards one merits Sh'mini Atzeres —
and then comes the "union of the Matron" (zivuga d'Matronissa):
Malchus receives the drops of intellect in completeness,
such that complete birth (holoda) is accomplished —
and [the seed of holiness] will not be, heaven forbid,
in the dimension of wasted emission (hashchasas zera l'vatala),
nor in the dimension of miscarriage (nafolim),
as is brought in the Kavanos — see there the depth of these matters and their secrets.

As it applies to us:
one merits to receive the light of the intellect and Wisdom in completeness,
to draw near through this to G-d in truth through all the things in the world —
this being the dimension of elevating all the sparks of Wisdom (nitzotzay chochma)
present in every thing;
and that one's deeds exceed one's wisdom;
and that one's fear of sin precedes one's wisdom;
and that the Wisdom and intellect be included and joined with
faith (emuna) and wholehearted simplicity (smimius).
This is the dimension of what is said of Yaakov specifically:
"And Yaakov was a wholesome man"
[Gen. 25:27]
— for this is the essential completeness of holy intellect,
which is the dimension of Yaakov.

And therefore it is explained in the holy Zohar
that on Sh'mini Atzeres, the quality of Yaakov our Father, a"h, shines most intensely,
and he is then "the head of the joy" — as mentioned above.
Therefore all Israel at that time ascend to the Torah,
complete the Torah, and begin the Torah again —
for the essential means to merit this is through the Torah, as above.

And This Is the Dimension of What the Sages Said…

And this is the dimension of what the Sages, z"l, said in the Zohar
and in the Tikunim:
"And the Ark rested in the seventh month"
[Gen. 8:4]
— regarding the topic of Tishray and Rosh HaShanah —
for then one draws down the dimension of the Tav-Nun-Ches
explained in the main text of the discourse,
which is the dimension of T'N'CH
[= Teshuva-Nun-Ches, or: the Ark rested — Vanach HaTaiva] as mentioned.

Translator's Summary — Siman 1

Siman 1 is based upon the discourse Ashray Smimay Dorech (Ps. 119:1) from Likutay Mohara"n.
The author reveals how Rosh HaShanah is fundamentally about the unification of
Chochma (Wisdom / Sun / Ches) with Malchus (Sovereignty / Moon / Nun) —
achieved through the Tzadik's work.
This theme then ripples forward through the entire month of Tishray:
the Ten Days of Repentance build the Malchus;
Yom Kippur perfects its union;
Sukkos teaches living in the "intellect" rather than material permanence (shade over sunlight);
the Four Species wave in all directions, proclaiming the inner divine intellect in all of Creation;
and Sh'mini Atzeres completes the sacred union — the Malchus receiving its fullness.
The centerpiece of all: being near the true Tzadik on Rosh HaShanah,
who alone can accomplish these rectifications in their completeness.

Siman 2 — Emor el HaKohanim ["Speak to the Priests" — Lev. 21]

Theme: Rosh HaShanah, Shofar, Prayer, and the Messiah

On Rosh HaShanah We Engage in the Shofar-Soundings to Drive Away the Husks

It is explained in Tikkunay Zohar, Tikkun 13, p. 36, that on Rosh HaShanah
one engages in the Shofar-soundings —
Tekia, Sh'vorim, Teruah —
to remove the husks (klippos) that cover and darken the light of the Keshes (Rainbow),
and through this, the light of the Messiah is drawn down.
And the sign of it is:
"Do not hope for the footsteps of the Messiah
until you see the rainbow in dazzling colors".

Because the very vitality of the Messiah is prayer —
and all his battles that he will wage,
and all the conquests he will conquer,
all come from there;
and his primary sword and bow is prayer and supplication —
therefore Israel at that time greatly multiply their prayers and supplications,
and pray extensively for the building of the holy Malchus
and the sprouting of the glory of David Your servant,
and the preparation of a lamp for the son of Yishai, Your anointed one, etc.

Because for this one needs the dimension of Yosef —
who is the dimension of guarding the Bris (covenant/holy bond) —
and also the dimension of Yaakov —
who is the dimension of Mishpot (justice/judgment) —
and justice is merited through Tzedaka (charity);
therefore one greatly increases [giving] charity at that time,
and prays extensively to rectify the blemish of the Bris.

And this is the dimension of going to the graves of Tzadikim on Erev Rosh HaShanah —
for the true Tzadikim are a great rectification for the blemish of the Bris,
as is understood in Likutay Mohara"n, Siman 109.

This is the dimension of HaMelech HaKadosh and Melech HaMishpot
["The Holy King" and "King of Justice"] which one says at that time —
for then one is engaged in building the Malchus
and the rectification of prayer,
which depends upon guarding the Bris —
for this is the very essence of holiness,
as the Sages, z"l, said: "Wherever you find [holiness]… there you find [the guarding of the]
Bris".
And one needs also the dimension of justice for this, as above.

This is the dimension of "Blow the Shofar in the month [of Tishray]"
— i.e., the Shofar-soundings of Rosh HaShanah —
and the verse concludes:
"for it is a statute for Israel — the judgment of the G-d of Yaakov"
[Ps. 81:5]
— hinting at guarding the Bris [chok] and the dimension of judgment of Yaakov,
as explained in the main text of this discourse above.
And this is the dimension of:
"A testimony in Yosef He placed it"
— and the Sages, z"l, expounded that on Rosh HaShanah, Yosef went out of prison —
and therefore the merit of Yosef, the dimension of guarding the Bris,
shines most intensely at that time.

The Three Blessings — Malchuyos, Zichronos, Shofaros

Malchuyos — corresponding to the dimension of the Kingdom of the Messiah,
whose very vitality comes from prayer, which is the dimension of Malchus, as is known,
and as is brought elsewhere.
Zichronos — corresponding to the dimension of Yosef,
the dimension of the Bris,
as is brought in the Zohar on the verse
"all your males shall appear before Me"
[Ex. 23:17]
— and this is the dimension of "He remembered His covenant forever"
[Ps. 111:5].
Shofaros — corresponding to the dimension of Yaakov,
the dimension of judgment, the dimension of
"the beauty of Yaakov"
[Lam. 2:1],
as is brought in the Zohar —
for through the sound of the Shofar, the essential quality and measure of Yaakov is aroused —
the dimension of justice —
and through this the essential rectification is accomplished.

And this is why the Sages, z"l, said:
"The horns of most animals are invalid for the Shofar
because they do not have an inner masculinity"
[Rosh HaShanah 26b]
— for the Shofar, which is the dimension of Yaakov,
must be included also from the dimension of Yosef —
the dimension of masculinity, the dimension of the Bris —
for Yaakov and Yosef go together as one,
as it is said:
"And the body and the covenant are considered one"
— and this is the essential substance of his progeny:
"These are the generations of Yaakov — Yosef"
[Gen. 37:2].

And therefore if one removed the masculinity (zichrus) of the Shofar and perforated it,
and blew through it — it is invalid —
for one also needs the dimension of justice, the dimension of Yaakov,
which is the Shofar itself.
And this is the dimension of the Teruah which is the dimension of Yaakov,
as is explained in the Zohar.
And Zichron Teruah [Remembrance of the Teruah — Lev. 23:24]
is when it is included also with the dimension of Yosef.

And this is said regarding Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbos —
when one mentions [the soundings] but does not actually blow the Shofar:
because the risk is that one might bring the Shofar into a public domain
[thereby desecrating the Shabbos],
and Shabbos desecration would be in the dimension of the quality of Yosef,
as is explained in the Zohar.
Therefore one does not blow —
rather, through the holiness of Shabbos itself
both dimensions shine —
for Shabbos is also in the dimension of the inheritance of Yaakov, as the Sages said.
Only in a place where there is a fixed Rabbinical court — such as in Yavneh —
where the dimension of justice which is the dimension of Yaakov shines more intensely,
does one blow even on Shabbos.

Because one must connect all prayers to the true Tzadik —
the dimension of Moshe —
for only he can illuminate and rectify the prayers of Israel in their completeness
and build from them the structure (koma) of the Divine Presence and the Sanctuary;
and he himself is in the dimension of the Messiah, as is explained —
therefore one must travel especially to the true Tzadik on Rosh HaShanah.

And because the letters of the Torah, which are the holy sparks of souls,
come and are included within prayer to be renewed there, etc. —
therefore one recites in the Rosh HaShanah prayers many verses
from the entire Tanach [Torah, Prophets, and Writings]
and verses regarding the Giving of the Torah, etc.

Afterwards One Engages in Repentance — Yom Kippur

Afterwards one engages in this throughout the Ten Days of Repentance —
for through repentance, the light of the Messiah is drawn down,
as is explained in Sefer HaMidos.
And the essence of repentance is through prayer and supplication —
the dimension of "Seek G-d when He may be found; call upon Him when He is near;
let the wicked forsake his way" etc.,
[Is. 55:6–7]
as the Sages, z"l, expounded —
until one merits on Yom Kippur.

Then Malchus, which is the very light of the Messiah,
is nourished only from the five voices —
the secret of the Five Afflictions and Five Prayers of Yom Kippur.
Then there is drawn most intensely the secret of the discourse we are engaged in:
that the very vitality of the Messiah is from prayer.
This is the secret of "from the Maid of the Palace she drew out a breath of life for the Messiah"
[Zohar, Teruma 177].

Because within the Pardashka mentioned above
is rooted the matter of the forgiveness of sin
and the overlooking of transgression,
and from there is rooted the sweetening of judgments —
as all of this is understood in the Zohar, Teruma p. 177, in the Sifra d'Tzniusa,
and in the Idra Rabba, Nasso, p. 136,
and in the Idra Zuta, p. 289 —
therefore on Yom Kippur is the essential sweetening of judgments and forgiveness of sins.

And then all the service [is performed] by the High Priest (Kohain Godol),
who is most holy in the holiness of the Bris —
for he is admonished even regarding a widow.
The Sages, z"l, expounded:
"With this shall Aharon enter"
[Lev. 16:3]
— in the merit of circumcision.
And the High Priest wears eight garments corresponding to the eight days of circumcision,
and he is the dimension of Aharon, who is the dimension of judgment (mishpot),
as is explained in the above discourse.

Then the dimension of the erection of the Sanctuary is drawn —
which is built from the prayers of Israel.
And therefore immediately on the day after Yom Kippur
they were commanded regarding the matter of the Sanctuary.
And also the dedication of the Temple of Solomon was on Yom Kippur.
Then the letters of the Torah are also renewed within prayer —
which is the dimension of what [the Sages taught]:
the completion of the reception of the Torah on the Second Tablets
was also on Yom Kippur,
as the Sages, z"l, expounded on the verse:
"On the day of his wedding"
[Song of Songs 3:11] — "this is the Giving of the Torah"
[Taanis 26b],
as the commentators have explained.

After Yom Kippur — The Loving-Kindnesses Enter

After Yom Kippur, the [supernal] loving-kindnesses (chassodim) begin to enter —
as is explained in the Kavanos —
the dimension of what the discourse concludes:
that even though it appears that through our prayers and Torah
the redemption will come,
nonetheless we need His loving-kindness —
for were it not for His kindness, we would have drowned, heaven forbid, in exile.
Therefore, after all the holy rectifications drawn through prayer and repentance
until Yom Kippur,
nonetheless the completion of salvation and rectification
is through the kindness of G-d — the dimension of the loving-kindnesses
that enter at that time.

And therefore one enters the Sukka,
which alludes to the Supernal Sukka — the dimension of Bina —
and to the Lower Sukka — the dimension of Malchus —
which is the dimension of Leah and Rachel.
These are the dimension of the seven Names:
72, 63, 45, 52, 161, 151, 143 —
their numerical value (gematria) is 689,
which is the gematria of Pardashka,
as brought in the writings of the Ar"i z"l.

And this is the dimension of Messiah Son of David,
who came specifically from Leah.
His essential vitality is from prayer,
which is itself included from both dimensions mentioned above —
the spoken words of prayer, and the intention (kavona) of the heart in prayer —
the dimension of "prepare their heart"
[Ps. 10:17], as the Sages said.

And see Siman 48 [of Likutay Mohara"n],
where it is also explained that the Sukka is the dimension of prayer with intention and strength.
This is the dimension of "the Sukka of David that has fallen"
[Amos 9:11]
— the dimension of the light of the Messiah who is called bar nofal [the fallen one].

The mitzvah of Sukka is a remembrance of the encompassing Clouds of Glory —
the dimension of the nullification of the clouds of the Stra Achra,
which are the dimension of alien thoughts
that nullify the intention of prayer, which is the dimension of [G-d's] honor (kovod),
as is explained in the main text.

The Four Species — Recalled and Praised within the Sukka

This is also the dimension of the Four Species —
which one takes and blesses within the Sukka as explained in the Kavanos —
and they allude to all the four groupings within Israel,
which is the dimension of the totality of the souls of Israel.

Afterwards one recites with them the Hallel prayer —
which is the dimension of the totality of the prayers of Israel,
containing past and future, etc., as the Sages, z"l, said.
And one also recites with them Hoshanos.
Therefore one waves [the four species] during "Give thanks to G-d"
and during "Please, G-d, save now"
— the dimension of the totality of prayers,
which is [G-d's] praise and the request for one's needs,
as is explained in the main text.

The primary blessing is on the taking of the lulav,
which is the tallest of all —
and alludes to the dimension of the Tzadik,
to whom all the groupings of Israel must attach themselves in their prayer.
The Tzadik is the dimension of Maor HaGodol — the Great Luminary —
and illuminates the esrog, which is the dimension of Maor HaKoton — the Small Luminary.

This is the dimension of "And you shall take for yourselves on the first day —
a fruit of a beautiful tree" etc. [Lev. 23:40],
and the Sages, z"l, expounded
that this is the dimension of
"all my bones shall say [G-d, who is like You]"
[Ps. 35:10]
— the dimension of the completeness of prayer —
for the lulav resembles the spine,
and this is the dimension of Yosef the Tzadik,
the dimension of Tzadik Chai Olamim — the Tzadik who is the life of the worlds —
the dimension of the eighteen vertebrae of the spine.
The esrog resembles the heart — the dimension of Messiah Son of David,
who is the heart of the world, as is understood in the story of the Seven Beggars.
Therefore it is called Hadar [beauty/adornment] —
the dimension of "splendor and glory You place upon him"
said of Messiah Son of David.

The hadas [myrtle] resembles the eyes — the dimension of judgment,
the dimension of "the eye of judgment"
— and the Sages, z"l, taught that the myrtle alludes to Yaakov,
who is the dimension of justice.
The arova [willow] resembles the lips — the dimension of prayer,
the dimension of "G-d, open my lips"
[Ps. 51:17];
and it also alludes to the letters of the Torah — the souls of Israel —
as it is said of them:
"And they shall sprout among the grass, like willows by streams of water"
[Is. 44:4].

Sh'mini Atzeres — The Sacred Union is Completed

Afterwards, on Sh'mini Atzeres,
comes the "union of the Matron" face to face —
the dimension of [the Zohar's] "when he warms with her, she turns",
as is explained in the main text.
The feminine [Malchus] retains the drop so that it does not miscarry —
for now, even though through prayer the structure (koma) of the Divine Presence is built,
it is only in the dimension of preparation for union —
the dimension of "we prepared and baked and cooked" [before Shabbos].
But even so, because the salvation is not yet complete,
one might err and say that the prayers produce no fruit —
the dimension of "we thought it was dry land".

But Sh'mini Atzeres alludes to the complete salvation that will come in the future —
when there will be the true union of the Matron face to face,
and every union and unification accomplished through the prayers of Israel
will be seen to have produced fruit and complete birth, as it were.
And then the joy is very great,
for the holy building is completed and the sacred, awe-inspiring union is accomplished —
which was engaged in during all the Days of Awe in their completeness.
And then also the letters of the Torah
that come within prayer are renewed and completed greatly —
this being the dimension of all Israel ascending to the Torah
and rejoicing greatly —
the dimension of:
"the maidens behind her, her companions, are brought to You;
they are led with joy and gladness"
[Ps. 45:15].
See the main text.

Translator's Summary — Siman 2

Siman 2 is based on the discourse Emor el HaKohanim (Likutay Mohara"n).
The central theme: the Messiah's entire life-force is prayer.
On Rosh HaShanah — through the Shofar soundings —
the husks covering the rainbow of the Messiah are removed.
The rectification requires the joining of two dimensions:
Yosef (the guarded Bris) and Yaakov (justice/judgment) —
hence visiting Tzadik's graves and increasing charity on Erev Rosh HaShanah.
The Three Blessings map precisely: Malchuyos = Messiah/Prayer; Zichronos = Yosef/Bris; Shofaros = Yaakov/Justice.
Yom Kippur is the apex of prayer-building (Five Prayers = Five Voices).
Sukkos and the Four Species encode the same structure — prayer, Bris, Tzadik-connection —
culminating in Sh'mini Atzeres when the union is perfected.

Siman 3 — Akroksa [A Talmudic term for a type of frog/creature — Zohar]

Theme: The Building of Holy Sovereignty and the Sacred Song

On Rosh HaShanah All Israel Engage in Building the Holy Kingdom

It is known that on Rosh HaShanah all Israel are engaged
in building the holy Malchus and nullifying the Malchus d'Stra Achra,
as one prays extensively for this in the Rosh HaShanah prayer service.

Because the birds (tzipporim) of the Stra Achra —
which are the mental faculties (mochin) of the Malchus d'Klipa [the husk-kingdom] —
are in the husk corresponding to the dimensions of Leah and Rachel,
as is explained in the holy writings —
therefore the intention of the Rosh HaShanah prayers
revolves around the matter of Leah and Rachel, as is explained there.

Because the flow of song and melody draws from the dimension
of the holy birds (tzipporim d'kedusha),
or [its opposite] from the side of evil, heaven forbid —
therefore one is exceedingly careful about the melodies of the Rosh HaShanah prayers —
that the prayer-leader (Shliach Tzibbur) be fitting and worthy —
and likewise regarding the one who blows the Shofar,
as is explained in the Shulchan Aruch.
For the Shofar soundings are also in the dimension of the voice of melody —
as it is written: "play well with the Teruah"
[Ps. 33:3].
And this is the dimension of: "A day of the Teruah shall it be for you"
— said of Rosh HaShanah.

And this is what the Sages, z"l, said:
"The Shofar-sounding is wisdom (chochma) and not a craft [melocha]"
[Rosh HaShanah 33b]
— for melody is from the dimension of Malchus.
This is the dimension of:
"for G-d is King of all the earth — sing a maskil"
[Ps. 47:8].
And this is "fortunate is the people who know the Teruah"
[Ps. 89:16]
— the Teruah is in the dimension of Daas (Knowledge) and the mental faculties.

Because the rectification of song and melody is through the Oral Torah (Torah SheBeal Peh),
therefore the Sages, z"l, taught in the Tikunim
that Teruah alludes to [the acronym]
T-O-R-A-H [Tav-Vav-Reish-Hay] — see the inner text [of the discourse] —
which is the dimension of the entire Oral Torah.
And therefore the Shofar soundings allude also to King David,
as is brought [in the Kabbalistic works] —
for he is in the dimension of the Oral Torah,
as is explained in Likutay Mohara"n, Siman 12.

This is also the dimension of Malchuyos, Zichronos, and Shofaros:
Malchuyos — the dimension of Malchus;
Zichronos — the dimension of the mental faculties and Daas,
as above in Siman 1;
Shofaros — the dimension of melody, as above.

And this is what is brought in the Zohar:
that the voice of the Shofar and the Teruah
corresponds to Yaakov —
for Yaakov merited to perfect this [holy] voice in its completeness,
the dimension of "the voice is the voice of Yaakov"
[Gen. 27:22].
He merited to rectify the dimension of the holy birds in their supernal root —
and this is the secret of [Yaakov] marrying the daughters of Lavan,
as is understood in the holy Zohar and in the writings of the Ar"i z"l.
And therefore the count of years of prophecy begins from Yaakov,
as brought in Megila Amukkos, Ofen 228.

Afterwards One Engages in Repentance — Yom Kippur

Afterwards one engages in this throughout all the Ten Days of Repentance —
greatly multiplying prayers and supplications,
and raising many holy voices —
the dimension of "from the depths I call to You, G-d; G-d, hear my voice"
[Ps. 130:1–2]
— until through this all the blemishes that were inflicted upon the holy Malchus are rectified,
until it returns and is rebuilt in completeness.
Until on Yom Kippur, Malchus is nourished only from five voices, etc. —
wherein is rooted the rectification of the holy voice above.
Then the High Priest enters "before and within"
[= the Holy of Holies],
where the Keruvim (Cherubs) and the holy birds are.
When Israel merited, the Keruvim faced one another —
and from them holy voices were heard —
and from this it was known that G-d had been fully appeased by Israel,
as brought in the holy Zohar.

After Yom Kippur — The Loving-Kindnesses Flow

After Yom Kippur the loving-kindnesses flow —
the dimension of [the Zohar's expression]
"how great is the force of the tree that is abundant",
as explained in the main text.
For through all the holy rectifications Israel drew in during the Ten Days of Repentance —
which are days of judgment, the dimension of night —
one thereafter merits to receive great loving-kindnesses
in the dimension of:
"one who studies Torah at night is drawn over with a thread of kindness by day"
[Avoda Zara 3b].

One merits to enter the Sukka —
which Israel merited in reward for Avraham our Father's saying to the angels:
"rest under the tree"
— the dimension of the eshel which Avraham planted,
which alludes to the loving-kindness (chesed) above, as explained in the main text.
This loving-kindness protects a person
so that the thought of doing a mitzvah not for its own sake (shelo lishmah)
does not harm him —
rather, on the contrary:
from within the shelo lishmah one will come to do it truly for its own sake (lishmah),
as the Sages, z"l, said.

And therefore it is required that stars be visible through the s'chach —
the dimension of what was said of Avraham:
"Look now toward the heavens and count the stars"
[Gen. 15:5],
and the Sages taught that He elevated him above the stars —
for [true] looking is always from above downward.

And because the essential drawing of this rectification is through Torah study at night specifically —
and night is the dimension of shade against the light of day —
therefore the shade of the Sukka must exceed its light.
And therefore the Sages derived the minimum height of the Sukka
from the Keruvim — the dimension of the holy birds mentioned above.

And this is the dimension of the joy of Sukkos,
and the primary joy was in Simchas Beis HaShoaiva [the Water-Drawing Celebration].
The Sages, z"l, taught that from there they drew forth the holy spirit —
meaning prophecy —
for from there is the source of the holy birds,
from the place where the prophets drew —
and from there is the building of the holy Malchus, the dimension of the Sukka of David.

And the Sages, z"l, said explicitly regarding prophecy:
"Prophecy does not rest upon a prophet except from within the joy of a mitzvah"
— as it is written: "and it was when the musician played"
[II Kings 3:15]
— specifically, "as the musician played" —
for prophecy and melody come from one source,
but they require a kosher and righteous musician specifically, as above.

The Four Species and the Patriarchs / Matriarchs

Peri Eitz Hadar [fruit of the beautiful tree] — this is Avraham —
the dimension of the loving-kindness of Avraham above.
Kapos Smorim [branches of date palms] — this is Yitzchok —
the dimension of judgment, the quality of night,
as it is written "and his eyes were dim"
[Gen. 27:1],
and as is explained elsewhere —
this is the dimension of Torah study at night specifically.
Anaf Eitz Avos [branches of a leafy tree] — this is Yaakov —
who merited the holy voice, the dimension of "the voice is the voice of Yaakov," as above.
Arvay Nachal [willows of the brook] — this is Yosef —
who merited sovereignty and the spirit of prophecy,
as it is written: "a man in whom there is the spirit of G-d"
[Gen. 41:38].
Therefore he is alluded to in arvay nachal
which alludes to the place from which the prophets draw, as is known.

[The Midrash] also expounded:
Peri Eitz Hadar — this is Sarah — the dimension of Malchus;
Kapos Smorim — this is Rivka,
as the date-palm has food and thorns,
so Rivka bore Yaakov and Esov.
Rivka is the dimension of Tvuna (Understanding/Applied Wisdom),
and therefore it is said:
"And Yitzchok was forty years old when he took Rivka"
[Gen. 25:20],
as is explained in Likutay Torah of the Ar"i z"l —
and there is the root of the Oral Torah.
Anaf Eitz Avos and Arvay Nachal allude to Leah and Rachel —
wherein is the root of the holy birds rectified completely by Yaakov, as above.

Sh'mini Atzeres — The Song is Completed

Afterwards one merits Sh'mini Atzeres —
and then the building of the holy Malchus is completed,
and therefore it is called Atzeres ["holding back"] —
the dimension of "this one holds back within himself",
as is explained in the Zohar.
And then the holy song is completed —
the dimension of "sing a maskil"
mentioned in the main text.
Then comes the union of the Matron, etc. —
for the essential connection and union of holiness is through the complete holy melody.
And therefore one greatly multiplies melodies, songs, and great joy [on Sh'mini Atzeres].

Translator's Summary — Siman 3

Siman 3 is drawn from the Akroksa discourse of Likutay Mohara"n.
The central insight: holy song and melody are the medium through which
the Malchus is built and the Stra Achra subdued on Rosh HaShanah.
The Shofar itself is a form of sacred melody — hence the requirement for a fitting, righteous Shofar-blower.
Yaakov perfectly rectified the dimension of holy song
(alluded to in his marriage to Lavan's daughters / the birds of Leah and Rachel).
Prophecy and song share one root.
The Four Species map to the Patriarchs and Matriarchs —
and all together point to the completion of holy song at Sh'mini Atzeres.

Siman 4 — Onochi ["I am [G-d your G-d]" — the first of the Ten Commandments]

Theme: Malchus, Confession before the Tzadik, and the Shofar-Soundings

On Rosh HaShanah We Engage in Building the Holy Sovereignty

On Rosh HaShanah one engages in building the holy Malchus
and the destruction of the rule of the nations (ummos haolam),
as we pray for this extensively on Rosh HaShanah.

Because this is impossible except through verbal confession (vidui d'vorim)
before a true Torah scholar (Talmid Chochom Amisi) —
who is the dimension of Moshe —
therefore one must be very careful to travel to the true Tzadikim on Rosh HaShanah;
or at the very least to pray at the graves of Tzadikim on Erev Rosh HaShanah,
as is explained in the Shulchan Aruch.
For "the Tzadikim are great in their death"
[Berachos 18b], etc. —
for then they are [absorbed], as it were, into the Infinite One [Ein Sof] completely.
And through the confessions one confesses at their graves,
and through the prayers and supplications one multiplies there —
through this, the Malchus is restored to its root,
meaning to the Will of the Infinite [Ein Sof],
as is explained in the main text.

Even on Rosh HaShanah Itself — One Confesses Softly

Therefore even on Rosh HaShanah itself —
when it is impossible to confess in a full, clear voice,
so as not to arouse the prosecutorial angels,
because of the great intensity of the judgments at that time —
nonetheless, even on Rosh HaShanah one must confess in a whisper at the very least.
And at the time of the Shofar-soundings, between one set and the next,
as is brought [in the Kavanos] —
for since the essential restoration of the Malchus to its root
is through verbal confession,
it is insufficient without it even on Rosh HaShanah.

Therefore one confesses at the time of the Shofar-sounding —
for then the essential engagement is in this:
to restore the Malchus to its root
and to build it as a complete new structure,
and to sweeten the judgments within the Name Elokim
through the Shofar, as is explained in the Kavanos.

And therefore through this, the Name Elokim is unified with the Name Havaya;
and G-d arises from the throne of judgment and sits upon the throne of mercy —
the dimension of "G-d ascends with the Teruah; G-d [goes up] with the sound of the Shofar"
[Ps. 47:6].
For through the Shofar-sound, the quality of Yaakov is aroused —
whose root is the Oral Torah.
And the Divine unity that is:
"G-d is the [same] G-d"
[I Kings 18:39]
— this is the dimension of the unity of loving-kindnesses and severe judgments —
the dimension of
"fortunate is the people that knows the Teruah"
[Ps. 89:16]
— "knows" specifically — the dimension of holy Daas.
And this Daas is a foretaste of the World to Come —
and this itself is the dimension of the Shofar,
which alludes to Bina (Understanding), the dimension of the World to Come.

And this is what [the Sages] said:
"Say Malchuyos before Me — so that you crown Me over you"
— the dimension of building the holy Malchus;
"Zichronos — so that your remembrance ascends before Me for good"
— the dimension of the sweetening of judgments at their root,
the dimension of "remember us for life, O King Who desires life"
— the opposite of the dimension of "the wrath of the King is the messenger of death"
[Prov. 16:14];
and therefore one does not recite Zichronos of [divine] punishment,
as the Sages, z"l, [taught].
And this is "And through what? Through the Shofar."

Therefore, through the Shofar-blowing and the repentance Israel performs then,
the Malchus is restored to its root in Wisdom,
which is absorbed into the Infinite —
as is explained in the Shla"h on the Kavona of the Shofar —
for the root of Malchus is in Wisdom:
"G-d established the earth with Wisdom"
[Prov. 3:19] —
"the Father founded the daughter", as is known.
And Wisdom is absorbed into the Infinite:
"and Wisdom — from whence is it found?"
[Job 28:12].
Therefore through the Shofar-blowing
one draws the sweetening of judgments —
the dimension of "and a wise man can appease it"
[Prov. 16:14], as is explained in the main text.

The Tekia-Terua-Tekia Pattern of the Baal Teshuva's Journey

This is the dimension of Tekia-Teruah-Tekia [which is from Torah law] —
for this is the way of the Baal Teshuva [one who returns to G-d]:
first G-d sends from above some illumination and flash of Infinite Light into his heart —
and through this he greatly regrets his deeds
and begins to engage in the rectifications of repentance,
until he merits afterward to cleave to G-d and to be absorbed in His Infinite Light
through arousal from below (isarusa d'lisata).

The first flash is in the dimension of the Tekia voice —
a simple sound —
for this illumination reaches him from G-d, Who is absolutely simple,
with no change whatsoever —
"I am G-d — I have not changed"
[Mal. 3:6].

Afterwards, what the person engages in —
the rectifications of repentance —
whose essence is through multiplying voices, cries, confessions, and supplications —
this is the dimension of Teruah:
"and when you go to war in your land… you shall sound a Teruah"
[Num. 10:9]
— the dimension of the war against the evil inclination,
which is the primary great war a person has in this world —
"and you shall sound it… and you shall be remembered before G-d your G-d"
— this is also the dimension of the Rosh HaShanah Shofar-sounding, as is brought in the Zohar.

And afterward one sounds a second simple Tekia —
meaning, through one's repentance
one restores the Malchus to its root —
the dimension of [the Zohar's]
"a spark that was cast to the place from which it was taken" —
and then one merits to return and to be absorbed in the Infinite
through isarusa d'lisata, as above.

And within this very matter there is also the dimension of Tekia-Teruah-Tekia:
The first Tekia is the dimension of being absorbed into the Infinite
in complete self-nullification (bitul gomur)
and in the dissolution of the physical —
to the point where one is in the dimension of
"and he did not know" —
even he himself does not know of himself —
for he is now at a supernal level and illumination such as this,
which is above the vessels of Daas and the mental faculties.
Afterwards, when one is in the dimension of Return (shov),
returning to one's awareness and selfhood —
this is the dimension of Teruah,
the dimension of Yaakov whose root is in Daas as above.
Within the dimension of selfhood there are variations of will
and variations of forms — this is the dimension of Teruah,
which is composed of many sounds — specifically Sh'vorim and Teruah,
which are "groaning-groaning and wailing-wailing"
— all of which pertain only to the dimension of selfhood.
Afterwards one returns to the simple Tekia —
for through the trace (reshimu) that remains in one's Daas
from the [experience of the] Infinite,
one demonstrates even to one's understanding
that one knows with complete knowledge
the unity of the Infinite and His goodness —
even when one is in the dimension of Return,
when one has returned from self-nullification to the dimension of selfhood,
one nonetheless knows with complete knowledge that it is all good, all one —
the dimension of "you have been shown to know that G-d — He is the G-d"
[Deut. 4:35].

And this is the essential completeness of Daas —
the dimension of the unity of loving-kindnesses and judgments.
And therefore [the Sages] taught:
every Teruah must have a simple [Tekia] before it and a simple [Tekia] after it —
for this is the essential completeness of Daas,
the dimension of Yaakov, the dimension of Teruah,
that it draw the simple unified Will of the light of the Infinite
into his Daas as well, as above.

Also, the first Tekia alludes to the connection and attachment to the Tzadik —
for Tekia is the language of connection ["they shook hands"] —
through which one merits to rectify all the character-traits of the four elements.
And this is the dimension of what is written regarding the trumpets (chatzotzros):
"And you shall blow them, and all the congregation shall assemble to you
at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting"
[Num. 10:3]
— from this it is clear that Tekia alludes to the holy journey of travel [to the Tzadik].
As it is written:
"And you shall blow a Teruah and they shall journey"
[Num. 10:5]
— this is the dimension whereby, through verbal confession before the Tzadik,
the Tzadik clarifies for one the straight path
according to the root of one's soul —
the dimension of [the traveler] who arrives at a crossroads
and then knows which path to travel.

And also Teruah alludes to the destruction of the rule of the nations —
this being the dimension of Sh'vorim:
"break the arm of the wicked"
[Ps. 10:15],
and likewise "G-d broke the staff of the wicked, the scepter of rulers"
[Is. 14:5].
And Teruah is also from the language of breaking —
"You shall break them with a rod of iron"
[Ps. 2:9].
And it alludes also to the building of the holy Malchus —
"G-d his G-d is with him, and the Teruah of the King is within him"
[Num. 23:21];
and as it is written:
"with trumpets and the sound of the Shofar shout before the King, G-d"
[Ps. 98:6].

And there is more to explain here regarding groaning-groaning and wailing-wailing
in the manner of what the Sages, z"l, taught:
"A sigh breaks half the body of a man"
— and this is a rectification for [the state where] one's sins were engraved upon one's bones,
as is explained in the main text.
The second Tekia alludes to being absorbed through this into the Light of the Infinite —
wherein all variations are subsumed into the simple unified Will, as above.
This is the dimension of:
"and when the congregation assembles, you shall blow but not sound the Teruah"
[Num. 10:7].

Afterwards One Engages in Repentance — Yom Kippur

Afterwards one engages throughout the Ten Days of Repentance in this —
to build the holy Malchus and restore it to its root,
which is the very essence of repentance —
the dimension of "Teshuva-Hay" [the Hay of repentance], as is known.
As is also understood in the discourse Ashray HaAm Zarka
in Likutay Mohara"n, Siman 35.
Until one merits on Yom Kippur to true forgiveness of sins —
and this was accomplished by Moshe our Teacher, a"h,
through his many prayers and supplications
throughout the last forty days of propitious times,
until on Yom Kippur G-d was appeased and forgave them their sin
and gave him the Second Tablets.
And from then on, this day was established as the [annual] atonement for sin throughout all generations,
as the Sages, z"l, taught.
And all through the dimension of "and a wise man can appease it," as above.

Therefore one multiplies confession in detail many times [on Yom Kippur] —
for the essential rectification is through verbal confession, as above —
through which one elevates Malchus — the dimension of Elokim —
to the Name Havaya,
and unity between the Name Elokim and the Name Havaya is accomplished.
And therefore one cries out many times at the conclusion of Yom Kippur:
"G-d — He is the G-d!"
[I Kings 18:39]

After Yom Kippur — The Loving-Kindnesses Enter

After Yom Kippur the loving-kindnesses enter —
which are the dimension of love and kindness —
meaning one merits to know
that all events are for the good,
whether mercy or judgment — all out of the love
that G-d has for us.
And through this itself, the judgments are sweetened —
until G-d truly conducts Himself toward us with great kindness and mercy.

And truly, the very fact that G-d chose us and loves us
and desires our love for Him —
and that we merit to cleave to Him and to be absorbed in His Infinite Light —
this loving-kindness surpasses all loving-kindnesses and all are included within it.

This is the dimension of the loving-kindness
that shines and is revealed on the first day of Sukkos —
which is the dimension of the Supernal Innermost Loving-Kindness (Chesed Elyon HaP'nimi)
and also the Supernal Encompassing Loving-Kindness.
And then all Israel enter the Sukka —
the shade of faith (tzila d'mehemnusa),
the dimension of "G-d is your shade at your right hand"
[Ps. 121:5].
And one merits at every moment to be absorbed in the Infinite Light —
and the Light of G-d enfolds, covers, and surrounds us,
and there all is surely one, all good, all kindness and mercy.

But because it is impossible to remain constantly in the state
of inclusiveness and self-nullification in the Infinite Light —
for one would be completely nullified from existence, heaven forbid —
therefore one must be in the dimension of
"running and returning" (ratzo v'shuv),
as is explained in the main text.
And this is the dimension of the Sukka as a temporary dwelling.

But because even in the dimension of Return (shuv)
— when one returns to one's awareness and selfhood —
the trace (reshimu) remains,
such that even to one's understanding it illuminates with the unity of the Infinite and His goodness —
therefore [the Sages] said:
all seven days a person makes the Sukka his primary [dwelling] and his house secondary.
For when one has tasted somewhat of the illumination of the Infinite,
one knows that the primary permanence of all is there.

And this is the essential completeness of the rectification of Malchus —
through loving-kindness,
the dimension of
"and through kindness a throne is established"
[Is. 16:5],
as is also brought in the Kavanos of Sukkos.

And this itself is the dimension of the Sukka —
for through this one raises it from its fall:
"I will raise up the Sukka of David that has fallen"
[Amos 9:11].

The Four Species — All Bones Shall Speak

The Sages, z"l, taught:
the esrog resembles the heart — the dimension of Malchus,
for "the heart in the body is like the King in war"
and "all the limbs conduct themselves after the heart, like a king".
The lulav resembles the spine — with the eighteen vertebrae —
the dimension of the Tzadik, the life of the worlds (Tzadik Chai Olamim) —
for the essential rectification of Malchus is through him.
The myrtle resembles the eyes —
the dimension of the rectification of the character-traits of all four elements —
through gazing at the Tzadik,
the dimension of:
"your eyes shall behold your teacher"
[Is. 30:20].
Also through the charity one gives him —
which is also the dimension of eyes — gazing upon the poor with merciful eyes.
The willow resembles the lips —
the dimension of the confession one confesses before the Tzadik,
telling him everything in one's heart.

Through all of this, the dimension of Malchus is rectified
and ascends to its root — where all is one, all good —
and the Name Havaya and the Name Elokim are unified in perfect unity.
And then certainly one merits to joy,
as is also understood in the discourse Vayomer Boaz, Siman 65.

This is the dimension of:
"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day"
and "you shall rejoice before G-d your G-d"
[Lev. 23:40]
— specifically, for the unity of G-d — He is the G-d is accomplished, as above.
And therefore the Hoshana prayers said with the lulav
conclude with the verse:
"so that all will know that G-d — He is the G-d".

And this is in merit of taking the four species on the first day:
"I will reveal Myself to you as the First"
— the dimension of the flash and illumination of the Infinite Light —
"and He pays back to you from the First — this is Esov"
— the nullification of the rule of the nations and the Stra Achra;
"and He builds for you the First — this is the Temple"
— the dimension of complete knowledge,
for the Sages, z"l, taught:
"Whoever possesses knowledge, it is as though the Temple was built in his days";
"and He brings for you the First — this is King Messiah"
— who will merit to the holy Malchus in total completeness.

Sh'mini Atzeres — The Building of Sovereignty is Complete

Afterwards, on Sh'mini Atzeres,
the building of the holy Malchus is completed —
and therefore it is called Atzeres ["holding back / gathering"] —
the dimension of "this one holds back within his people",
as brought in the Zohar.
Then the union of the Matron [takes place],
the sovereignty returns to G-d alone —
the dimension of "and he shall say, all that has breath in its nostrils:
G-d, the G-d of Israel, is King, and His sovereignty reigns over all".
And through this one merits to complete knowledge —
a foretaste of the World to Come,
when all will be one, all good.
And therefore Sh'mini Atzeres is only one day and alludes to the World to Come, as is brought.

And because the Torah is the dimension of the root of Malchus —
"through Me kings reign"
[Prov. 8:15]
— therefore in Eretz Yisroel the Torah is completed [at that time]
and recommenced from the beginning.

And because the true Torah scholars are the dimension of Moshe —
engaged in the rectification of the holy Malchus
and the humbling of the Malchus d'Stra Achra,
both during their physical lifetimes
and especially after their passing —
when they ascend and are absorbed into the Light of the Infinite —
this is the dimension of what is said of Moshe our Teacher, a"h:
"And He buried him in the valley in the land of Moav
opposite Beit Peor"
[Deut. 34:6],
as is explained in the main text.
This is the dimension of what the beginning of the preparation for the holy building
— which Israel engages in from Rosh HaShanah to Sh'mini Atzeres —
is going on Erev Rosh HaShanah to the graves of Tzadikim, as above.
Therefore the Torah is completed with those verses describing the passing of Moshe:
"which Moshe performed before the eyes of all Israel"
[Deut. 34:12]
— and the Sages, z"l, taught that this refers to his breaking the Tablets before their eyes.

And immediately after the conclusion of the Torah,
one begins again with Bereishis bara Elokim —
"In the beginning G-d created" —
for all was created only for the revelation of His sovereignty.
And the revelation of His sovereignty is through Israel and through the holy Torah,
which is the root of Malchus.
And therefore the Sages taught:
"Bereishis — for the sake of Israel,
and for the sake of the Torah,
and for the sake of Moshe"
— for he is the primary one engaged in this.

And immediately [the Torah] alludes to the rule of the nations —
the dimension of "and the earth was void and formless" etc.
— the Sages, z"l, [expounded] this of the four [exile-]kingdoms.
And "the spirit of G-d hovered" etc. —
this is the spirit of the Messiah,
the very dimension of the holy Malchus.
And "G-d said: Let there be light"
— and "there was evening and there was morning — one day"
— that G-d will be One and Singular in the world,
as the Sages, z"l, expounded —
for this is the essential completeness of the rectification of Malchus:
when His unity is revealed in the world
and one merits to the dimension of all-good, all-one —
the dimension of:
"And G-d shall be King over all the earth;
on that day G-d shall be One and His Name One"
[Zech. 14:9].

The Great Joy of Sh'mini Atzeres

And this is the dimension of the great joy with which Israel rejoice at that time —
for through the dimension of all-one, all-good,
one merits great joy, as above.
Also, because the primary joy is over the revelation of His sovereignty
which is drawn at that time —
the dimension of:
"Israel shall rejoice in its Maker;
the children of Tzion shall exult in their King"
[Ps. 149:2],
and "the heavens shall rejoice and the earth shall be glad,
and they shall say among the nations: G-d reigns"
[I Chron. 16:31].

And this itself is the matter explained in the Kavanos of Sh'mini Atzeres —
that the [feminine principle] retains the drop so that it does not miscarry:
for sometimes a person merits that some flash of the Infinite Light opens for him —
but he does not merit that the trace of it should illuminate him afterward
when he is in the dimension of Return —
and this is like the dimension of miscarriage, heaven forbid.
But when one merits that even after returning from self-nullification to the dimension of selfhood,
the trace of the unity of the Infinite still shines —
this is the dimension of not miscarrying.

Translator's Summary — Siman 4

Siman 4 maps the Tekia-Teruah-Tekia structure of the Shofar onto the Baal Teshuva's spiritual journey.
The first Tekia = G-d's initial flash of illumination.
The Teruah = the person's cries, confessions, and battle against the evil inclination.
The final Tekia = the soul's return and reabsorption into the Infinite.
Within the Teruah itself: Sh'vorim = groaning (the quality of mercy/Yosef); Teruah = shattering (the quality of justice/Yaakov).
The first Tekia also alludes to connecting to the Tzadik — hence traveling to him on Rosh HaShanah.
The same three-stage pattern governs the entire month: Rosh HaShanah (Tekia) → Ten Days / Yom Kippur (Teruah) → Sukkos through Sh'mini Atzeres (Tekia of completion).

Siman 5 — BaChatzotzros ["With Trumpets" — Num. 10]

Theme: Clothing Prayer in Narrative Praise; The Three Blessings as Garments

Rosh HaShanah — The Birthday of Creation

Rosh HaShanah is the first day of the creation of the world —
"This is the day, the first of Your works, a remembrance of the first day".
On it was created the first Adam, who was the purpose of all creation —
he was to engage in the rectification of the world
and to fill the lack of the world
and to pray on their behalf,
as Rashi, z"l, explains on the verse:
"and there was no man to work the soil"
[Gen. 2:5].
But the serpent came and enticed Chava,
and what happened happened —
he was judged and went out acquitted (b'dimusos).
And from then on, this day was established as Rosh HaShanah —
the Day of Judgment — for all generations, as the Sages, z"l, taught.

And on every Rosh HaShanah the dimension of the renewal of creation is drawn —
and every person must say:
"the entire world was created only for my sake"
[Sanhedrin 37a]
— and he must see and reflect on the rectification of the world,
on filling its lacks, and on praying on its behalf.

Because of the great intensity of the judgments on Rosh HaShanah,
one must clothe the prayer in narrative (maamar)
so that the [prosecutorial] angels standing on the left should not accuse.
And this is why the Sages, z"l, established
to pray for life at that time in the first three blessings —
which are [G-d's] praise —
as one prays "Remember us" and "Who is like You"
not in the wording of petition and request,
but in the manner of praise and thanksgiving.

And also in the last three blessings one says: "inscribe" etc.,
"in the Book of Life" etc.
— which is not done throughout the rest of the year,
as the legal authorities have noted carefully.
All of this is in order to clothe the prayer, to conceal it,
and to include it within [G-d's] praise —
so that the [accusers] do not accuse.

And therefore one must be extra careful at that time
not to multiply requests for one's material needs —
but rather to pray primarily for matters of spirit,
as is brought in the holy books.
And therefore one multiplies prayers primarily for
the revelation of His sovereignty and that
"G-d's glory fill all the earth"
[Ps. 72:19]
— for over prayers such as these the [accusers] cannot accuse greatly,
since all is only for His honor.
And within this one includes also prayers and requests
for the elevation of the glory of Israel, their salvation and success,
and the nullification of the Malchus d'Stra Achra —
all in order to clothe the prayer and conceal and veil it, as above.

Therefore in the Musaf prayer —
where one speaks at length —
but all is only in the manner of narrative and telling of His praises —
and within this one seizes and includes also the prayer and request that one needs.
And this is what we say in Malchuyos: Alaynu l'shabayach
["It is upon us to praise…"]
— and one multiplies verses from Torah, Prophets, and Writings —
and within this one includes also the prayer and request,
concluding: "Reign over all the world" etc.
Likewise in Zichronos one begins in the manner of narrative and praise:
"You remember the works of the world" etc.,
multiplies verses, and concludes: "Remember us with a good remembrance" etc.
Likewise in Shofaros one begins:
"You were revealed" etc., and concludes:
"Sound the great Shofar" etc.

And all of this in order to clothe the prayer
and to include it within [G-d's] praise
and within the recitation of verses of Torah —
so that the [accusers] do not accuse.
This is the dimension of what is explained in the main text:
that after a divine decree one must clothe the prayer in narrative (maamar).
Similarly this is required on Rosh HaShanah
because of the great intensity of the judgments and accusations that intensify at that time.

And this is what the Sages, z"l, taught:
"Say Malchuyos before Me on Rosh HaShanah so that you crown Me over you"
— specifically "say before Me" —
hinting at the fact that the primary substance of the recitations of Malchuyos, Zichronos, and Shofaros
are in the manner of narrative and telling,
which is the dimension of clothing prayer in narrative, as above.

Because the way of how to clothe prayer in narrative —
how to do this in its completeness —
is known only to Tzadikim,
as is understood in the main text
regarding the verse "and by the word of the holy ones the matter is settled"
[Dan. 4:14],
and also regarding the verse "they together make the mountains sing"
[Is. 44:23] —
therefore one must be especially careful to come on Rosh HaShanah to the Tzadikim
and to pray with them.

One Must Guard Awe, Protect the Mind, and Unite Love with Awe

Because for this matter one merits only through performing mitzvos with joy —
such complete joy that one does not desire any reward of the World to Come for it,
but rather that the reward be in the mitzvah itself;
and the primary joy is in the heart —
and the heart cannot rejoice until one removes the crookedness of the heart
and one has straightness of heart (yishrus lev) —
and for this one merits through prayer with force and awe of Heaven.

This is the dimension of the "thunders" (r'omim) —
the voice emerges from mighty judgments (g'voros), the dimension of awe,
and strikes the mental faculties.
Then the heart hears — and the sound is heard by all creatures —
and these are the thunders which are from the side of Yitzchok —
the dimension of the voice of the Shofar and the Teruah.

But for this one must guard the awe
so that it does not become external awe [merely a show];
and to guard the mental faculties from "leavening" (chametz) —
that one's wisdom not be leavened by external wisdoms, desires, and alien thoughts;
and one must also blend the judgments with loving-kindnesses —
meaning, love together with awe.
For the essential revelation is through loving-kindnesses —
the dimension of:
"Avraham who loves Me"
[Is. 41:8]
who gave his life for the sanctification of His Name.

"And so grant Your fear" [Uv'chein tain pachdecho] —
this corresponds to the rectification of awe,
and is therefore directed toward Yitzchok — Pachad Yitzchok [the Fear of Yitzchok].
Because one must blend the judgments with loving-kindnesses —
which are the dimension of the Right —
one therefore says there: "and might is in Your right hand".

"And so grant honor" [Uv'chein tain kovod] —
this corresponds to Yaakov,
who merited the holy voice mentioned above —
the dimension of "the voice is the voice of Yaakov" —
the voice that emerges from the judgments and strikes the mental faculties,
which are the dimension of honor (kovod), as is explained in the main text.
For Yaakov our Father's root is in Daas and the mental faculties, as is known.

And through all of this one merits to joy —
the dimension of:
"And so the Tzadikim shall see and rejoice, and the upright shall exult" etc.
— specifically "the upright" — the dimension of "and for the upright of heart — joy."
And this is "And so [David]" [Uv'chein] — the dimension of Malchus —
the dimension of prayer —
for through all of this prayer is complete.

And this is the dimension of the Rosh HaShanah Shofar-sounding —
through which the dimension of "thunders" is drawn,
until one merits to joy —
the dimension of "in Your Name they shall rejoice all day"
[Ps. 89:17],
and likewise:
"for the joy of G-d is your strength"
— said also of Rosh HaShanah
[Neh. 8:10].
And this is what one blesses: "to hear the voice of the Shofar" —
for this is the essence of the mitzvah:
to hear this voice within one's heart thoroughly —
until the crookedness of the heart dissolves
and one merits straightness of heart.

And therefore the Shofar-soundings also correspond to Avraham, Yitzchok, Yaakov, and David,
as is brought —
the dimension of all the rectifications mentioned above.

And because the essential [requirement] is to guard one's mind from "leavening" —
which is the secret of the removal of chametz and the eating of matza on Pesach,
as is understood in the main text —
as is explained in the Zohar, Shmos, p. 183b,
that the primary accusation on Rosh HaShanah
concerns those who were not careful about chametz on Pesach —
therefore one prays at that time: "Remember us for life"
and many similar prayers — the opposite of chametz, which is the side of death, heaven forbid.
And therefore on Rosh HaShanah one must be extra careful
about the purity of thought (k'dushas hamachshova),
as is explained elsewhere.

And this too is the topic of the Ten Days of Repentance, Yom Kippur, Sukkos, and Sh'mini Atzeres —
all revolving around what is explained in this discourse above,
as is explained somewhat in Likutay Halachos,
Laws of Established Ownership (Chezkas Karkos), Law 3 — see there,
and one needs to elaborate upon it further.

Translator's Summary — Siman 5

Siman 5 introduces the concept of clothing prayer in narrative praise on Rosh HaShanah —
because the judgments are so intense that direct petitions invite prosecution from the accusing angels.
The entire structure of the Rosh HaShanah prayer service — Malchuyos, Zichronos, Shofaros —
is designed as a sacred garment: praise on the outside, prayer hidden within.
Only the true Tzadik knows how to perfectly accomplish this cloaking,
which is why being near a Tzadik on Rosh HaShanah is so essential.
The discourse concludes by mapping the three liturgical blessings
Uv'chein onto Avraham/Yitzchok/Yaakov/David —
joy, awe, straightness of heart, and holy kingship.
