Siman 7 — V'Aileh HaMishpatim ["And These are the Judgments" — Ex. 21]

Theme: Faith, Truth, and Rosh HaShanah as the Renewal of Creation

On Rosh HaShanah the Renewal of Creation is Drawn

On Rosh HaShanah the dimension of the renewal of creation is drawn —
the dimension of:
"This is the day, the first of Your works, a remembrance of the first day".
The primary creation was through the virtue of Emuna (faith) —
as it is written: "and all His deeds are in faith"
[Ps. 33:4],
as is explained elsewhere.

But the essential completeness of Emuna is through Emes (truth).
And to truth one merits through drawing near to Tzadikim and following their guidance.
But against this there is the dimension of the counsel of the serpent —
the dimension of the unclean union (nissuim d'klippa), heaven forbid —
as is explained in the main text.

And this was the blemish of Adam on Rosh HaShanah —
on the very first day in which he was created
and commanded regarding the Tree of Knowledge.
Within this commandment were included all 613 mitzvos of the Torah — all holy counsels.
But through the counsel of the serpent, he transgressed the commandment —
was judged — and went out acquitted.
And from then on it was established for all generations
that Rosh HaShanah would be the Day of Judgment —
as the Sages, z"l, said.

And Israel engages in the rectification of this matter every year
from Rosh HaShanah to Sh'mini Atzeres, as is explained in the Kavanos.
And this is the dimension of engaging in building the holy Malchus at that time —
to establish and build the holy faith (Emuna),
which is itself the dimension of Malchus, as is known —
and it is the dimension of prayer, miracles, and the Land of Israel.
All of these rectifications are drawn on Rosh HaShanah.

And therefore one multiplies prayer at that time for this very matter —
that the holy faith spread throughout the world,
and the redemption draws near through the King Messiah —
for upon this the redemption depends.
And that the holiness of Eretz Yisroel, Tzion, and Yerushalayim be revealed.

Also on Rosh HaShanah the dimension of miracles and the nullification of nature is drawn —
for the root of the governance of nature derives from the dimension of the concealment of the Divine Countenance (hester ponim),
the dimension of judgment —
for Elokim has the same numerical value as ha-Teva [nature].
And on Rosh HaShanah one is primarily engaged in sweetening the judgments —
which is the dimension of miracles above nature.

And therefore the Sages, z"l, in the Yerushalmi of Rosh HaShanah, Chapter 1,
expressed astonishment:
"Since Israel knows that Rosh HaShanah is the Day of Judgment,
nonetheless they don white clothing, etc., and eat and drink and rejoice —
knowing that G-d performs miracles for them" — as mentioned above.

Also, the holiness of Eretz Yisroel — where the primary miracles [occur] —
is drawn primarily from the holiness of Rosh HaShanah,
as it is written:
"the eyes of G-d your L-rd are upon it, from the beginning of the year"
[Deut. 11:12].

And this is the dimension of what was established by the early authorities
to recite V'Chol Maaminim ["And All Believe"] on Rosh HaShanah —
for this is the primary engagement at that time: to complete the holy faith.

And because the completeness of faith is through truth —
and this too must be drawn on Rosh HaShanah,
which is the dimension of the beginning of creation, which was through truth —
as it is written:
"In the beginning, G-d created"
— the final letters [of the first three words in Hebrew]: Aleph-Mem-Tav = Emes [truth].
And the Sages, z"l, expounded on this:
"The beginning of Your word is truth"
[Ps. 119:160].

And this itself is the matter of Rosh HaShanah on which Rosh Chodesh also falls —
the dimension of the joining of Emes [truth — the dimension of the year]
with Emuna [faith — the dimension of the month].
And where the male and female are [united in truth], the male is not mentioned separately —
therefore Rosh Chodesh is not mentioned on Rosh HaShanah.

And because it is impossible to come to truth except through drawing near to Tzadikim
and walking in the way of their guidance —
therefore one must travel to the Tzadikim on Rosh HaShanah,
or at the very least to pray at the graves of Tzadikim on Erev Rosh HaShanah —
in order to draw upon oneself their strength and holiness.

They merited the dimension of guarding the Bris —
after which they are called Tzadikim, as is known.
And guarding the Bris is the dimension of the holy union (nissuim d'kedusha),
the dimension of holy counsels —
through which one merits to truth,
until through this the holy faith is completed,
and one merits to the eternal redemption —
which is the essential engagement of Rosh HaShanah, as above.

And because faith and prayer are in the dimension of miracles —
and are propitious for remembrance — as is explained in the main text —
therefore Rosh HaShanah is called Yom HaZikaron — "The Day of Remembrance."

This is the dimension of Malchuyos, Zichronos, and Shofaros.
As the Sages, z"l, said:
"Say Malchuyos on Rosh HaShanah so that you crown Me over you"
— the dimension of building Malchus and rectifying faith and prayer.
"Zichronos — so that your remembrance ascends before Me for good"
— the dimension of the nullification of judgments and of nature,
from which derives the dimension of forgetfulness, as it were —
as it is written:
"How long will You forget me forever?"
[Ps. 13:2].
And the more one merits to nullify the forgetfulness
and attain the holy remembrance,
one can certainly be confident that one's remembrance ascends before G-d for good.
For truly there is no forgetfulness before the Throne of His Glory,
as one recites in the blessing of Zichronos.

And this is the dimension of
"fortunate is the man who does not forget You"
— said at that time.
And "through what? Through the Shofar" —
for the Shofar-sound alludes to the quality of Yaakov,
whose quality is truth;
and through this, faith is completed
and one merits complete knowledge and holy remembrance, as is understood in the main text.

And this is the dimension of Zichron Teruah ["A Remembrance of the Teruah"] —
for Teruah is the dimension of Yaakov, as is explained in the Zohar —
for Yaakov merited to rectify the blemish of Adam the first man
and to nullify the impurity of the serpent,
as is brought in the Zohar.
And therefore he merited guarding the Bris in ultimate completeness —
as it is written:
"the first-fruits of my strength"
[Gen. 49:3],
and from him was born Yosef the Tzadik,
who merited guarding the Bris completely, as is explained in the main text.

And therefore all Israel — who are in the dimension of "wholly a seed of truth" —
are called by the name of Yosef:
"He leads Yosef like sheep"
[Ps. 80:2].
And therefore in the Exodus from Egypt it was said:
"You shall bring up my bones from here with you"
[Gen. 50:25].
And likewise:
"And Moshe took the bones of Yosef with him"
[Ex. 13:19]
— for through the dimension of Yosef, the faith was completed,
upon which the redemption depends.
And the Sages, z"l, taught
that even the bones of the other tribes were elevated with them —
for the tribes are the dimension of the twelve texts of prayer, as is explained in the main text —
they are the dimension of faith;
they are the dimension of the twelve oxen upon which the "Sea of Solomon" rested —
the dimension of the sovereignty of Heaven, which is the dimension of faith —
all were completed and elevated through the bones of Yosef,
the dimension of the grave of the true Tzadik.
Therefore the custom is to go on Erev Rosh HaShanah to the graves of Tzadikim —
for on Rosh HaShanah the dimension of the redemption of Pesach begins to shine.
Therefore on Rosh HaShanah Yosef went out of prison —
and on Rosh HaShanah the enslaved labor of our ancestors in Egypt ceased, as the Sages, z"l, said.

Afterwards — The Ten Days of Repentance

Afterwards one engages in this throughout the Ten Days of Repentance —
for this is the essential repentance: for not having fulfilled the 613 counsels
through which the holy faith is completed —
the general principle of all of them,
as it is written:
"all Your commandments are faith"
[Ps. 119:86].
Rather, on the contrary —
we were ensnared by the counsel of the wicked, the dimension of the impurity of the serpent,
and we blemished the holy faith —
and through this we were exiled from our land and came to where we have come.

And on the Ten Days of Repentance one engages in rectifying this —
and then prayer is received most intensely,
as it is written: "Seek G-d when He may be found"
[Is. 55:6],
as the Sages, z"l, expounded.
And therefore they are Ten Days of Repentance
corresponding to the ten holiness levels with which Eretz Yisroel was sanctified,
and to the Ten Utterances of the world's creation — the essence of holy faith —
and to the Ten Commandments — the entirety of the holy Torah through which faith is completed —
and to the ten expressions by which prayer is called, as the Sages, z"l, said —
and corresponding to the ten miracles wrought for our ancestors in Egypt and at the Sea,
and to the ten miracles wrought for our ancestors in the Temple —
for there is the source of the holiness of Eretz Yisroel, the place of miracles —
until one merits afterward to the holiness of Yom Kippur,
when faith is completed in the dimension of the "pinnacle of faith" (rosh emuna).

And therefore on Yom Kippur there is forgiveness of sins,
as is explained in Sefer HaMidos, under Emuna:
through faith, G-d will forgive your sins.
And this is a full scriptural verse:
"wander through the streets of Jerusalem…
if there be one who acts with justice, who seeks truth — I will forgive this one"
[Jer. 5:1].
And then prayer is completed — this being the dimension of the Five Prayers of Yom Kippur.
And then the dimension of miracles is drawn — the sweetening of judgments at their root —
which is the essence of miracles.
And indeed in a simple sense there were many miracles — in the lot that was cast,
in the scarlet thread that would turn white,
and that no improper emission befell the High Priest on Yom Kippur —
and likewise other things the Sages, z"l, enumerated.

And then the inner holiness of Eretz Yisroel is revealed —
this being the dimension of the High Priest entering the innermost [sanctuary] —
for from there is the source of all the holiness of Eretz Yisroel.
And then Moshe descended with the Second Tablets —
the sum of the holy Torah — 613 holy counsels — the dimension of truth —
through which the holy faith is completed.
And then the serpent was subdued and its impurity
completely nullified in Israel —
this being the dimension of what [the Sages taught]:
on Yom Kippur the Accuser has no authority to prosecute.

And because through the mitzvah of tzitzis a person is saved from the counsel of the serpent
and merits all the above —
therefore on Yom Kippur one wraps oneself in tzitzis [from before sunset] —
and all of Yom Kippur Israel stands wrapped in tzitzis.

After Yom Kippur — Sukkos: The Loving-Kindnesses Enter

After Yom Kippur the loving-kindnesses begin to enter,
and through them faith — the dimension of Malchus — is rectified most fully,
as is brought in the holy writings:
that the essential rectification of Malchus is through loving-kindnesses —
the dimension of "and through kindness a throne is established"
[Is. 16:5].
And therefore Avraham our Father — the man of loving-kindness —
was the first among believers,
as is also understood in the discourse Bini Lon Baisa, Siman 28.

And likewise the essential miracles flow through loving-kindnesses —
"to the One Who performs great wonders alone — for His kindness is eternal"
[Ps. 136:4].
And likewise the essential prayer is through loving-kindnesses —
"blessed is G-d Who has not removed my prayer and His kindness from me"
[Ps. 66:20].
And likewise the inheritance of Eretz Yisroel is through loving-kindnesses —
"an inheritance to Israel His servant — for His kindness is eternal"
[Ps. 136:21–22].
And likewise truth is merited through loving-kindnesses —
"grant truth to Yaakov, kindness to Avraham"
[Mic. 7:20].
And likewise drawing near to the Tzadik and receiving his guidance is in the dimension of loving-kindnesses.
And likewise the entire holy Torah is called Toras Chesed — the Torah of Kindness.
And likewise the essential redemption is through loving-kindnesses.

Then One Enters the Sukka — The Union of Truth and Faith

Then one enters the Sukka,
and the loving-kindnesses shine in a wondrous light —
and the union of Emes [truth] and Emuna [faith] is completed —
they being the dimension of man and woman —
this being the dimension of the Sukka,
whose letters spell out Kuf-Vav = 26 and Hay-Samech = 65
[= the numerical values of the Names Havaya and Adnay],
as is explained in the holy Zohar.
And therefore the Sages, z"l, taught:
"You shall dwell as you normally dwell — a man and his wife"
[Sukkah 28b],
as is explained in the Shulchan Aruch.

Then a great illumination flows from the dimension of the Supernal Bina to the heart —
which is the dimension of the Supernal Sukka
to the Lower Sukka, the dimension of the Sukka of David, the dimension of Malchus.
For the root of counsel (aitza) is in the dimension of Bina to the heart —
as it is written:
"deep waters are counsel in a person's heart"
[Prov. 20:5].
And there is the root of truth —
"and one who speaks truth in his heart"
[Ps. 15:2].
And therefore the entire holy Torah emerges from there,
as is understood in Siman 266, the discourse Vayaakov Nosa Sukkosa.
And through all of this the holy faith is completed —
and one merits the complete redemption —
the dimension of:
"I will raise up the Sukka of David that has fallen"
[Amos 9:11].

And this is the dimension of the four species:
Peri Eitz Hadar — this is Avraham —
the dimension of faith —
as it is written: "and he believed in G-d"
[Gen. 15:6]
— and he was first among believers.
Kapos Smorim — this is Yitzchok —
the dimension of prayer —
for the Sages, z"l, taught that Yitzchok mastered the craft of prayer;
and the Sages, z"l, said: "A person should always be diligent in the afternoon prayer (Mincha)"
— and Yitzchok established the Mincha prayer.
Anaf Eitz Avos — this is Yaakov —
the dimension of truth, as above.
Arvay Nachal — this is Yosef —
the dimension of guarding the Bris, guarding against the counsel of the wicked —
the dimension of licentiousness (niuf), heaven forbid.

And also [the Midrash] expounded:
Peri Eitz Hadar — this is Sarah, the dimension of Malchus, the dimension of faith —
the Sages, z"l, taught: just as Avraham converted [brought people to faith] and publicized faith in the world, so too did Sarah.
Kapos Smorim — this is Rivka — also the dimension of prayer —
as it is written:
"and Yitzchok prayed to G-d opposite his wife"
[Gen. 25:21]
— and the Sages, z"l, taught: she stood in the corner and prayed.
Anaf Eitz Avos — this is Leah —
the dimension of miracles:
the Sages, z"l, taught that Leah was the first to give thanks —
the dimension of Al HaNissim ["For the Miracles"]
that one says in the blessing of thanksgiving (Hoda'a).
Also, by natural law Leah was destined to fall to the portion of Esov —
but through her many tears
G-d performed miracles for her and she fell to the portion of Yaakov.
Arvay Nachal — this is Rachel —
the secret of the holiness of Eretz Yisroel, as is explained in the Zohar and the writings of the Ar"i z"l.
And therefore Yehoshua, who descended from her children's children,
was the one who gave us our inheritance in Eretz Yisroel.

The Four Species — Joy

And therefore these four species atone for the rains that come from the depths — the dimension of miracles —
for the primary rains in Eretz Yisroel are explained in the main text.
And this is the dimension of the joy with the four species —
"and you shall rejoice before G-d your G-d"
[Lev. 23:40]
— for all these dimensions are themselves the dimension of joy:
Faith which is the dimension of Malchus is joy —
"G-d reigns, the earth shall rejoice"
[Ps. 97:1].
Prayer is joy — "serve G-d with joy"
— and there is no service but prayer.
Miracles are joy — "this is the day G-d has made; we shall rejoice and be glad in it"
[Ps. 118:24].
Eretz Yisroel is joy —
"beautiful of height, the joy of the entire earth"
[Ps. 48:3].
The redemption is joy —
"when G-d returned the captivity of Tzion… we were as dreamers"
— joyful.
Drawing near to the Tzadik is joy —
"when the Tzadikim increase, the people rejoice"
[Prov. 29:2].
The counsel of the Tzadik is joy —
"and for those who counsel peace — joy"
[Prov. 12:20].
And the 613 counsels of the Torah —
"the statutes of G-d are upright, gladdening the heart"
[Ps. 19:9].
The judgments of G-d — truth — are joy —
"it is joy for the Tzadik to do justice"
[Prov. 21:15].

Sh'mini Atzeres — The Union of Truth and Faith is Complete

Afterwards one merits Sh'mini Atzeres
— then the union of the Matron —
the dimension of [the Zohar's expression that]
man and woman are equalized,
as is explained in the main text —
meaning: the dimensions of truth and faith are unified in ultimate perfect union.
And the feminine [Malchus] retains the drop so that it does not miscarry —
meaning one merits to receive the drops of intellect and mind of the true Tzadikim
and of the entirety of our holy Torah in ultimate completeness,
in an enduring bond —
so that one thereby merits to produce good and holy fruits and offspring in ultimate completeness.

And this is the dimension of what is explained in the Kavanos:
that the birth from the sacred union of Sh'mini Atzeres
is realized from the Seventh Day of Pesach —
when the completion of the Exodus from Egypt, which includes all exiles, took place.
And what is accomplished is what will be accomplished —
for in every generation and every year this dimension is drawn,
until one thereby merits the complete redemption, speedily in our days.

And therefore the joy of Sh'mini Atzeres is exceedingly great —
and Yaakov our Father is the "head of joy" at that time,
as is explained in the Zohar —
for all the rectifications mentioned above are completed through "grant truth to Yaakov," as above.

Translator's Summary — Siman 7

Siman 7 uncovers the hidden theme of Rosh HaShanah as the renewal of creation —
grounded in the virtue of Emes (Truth) joined with Emuna (Faith).
Adam's sin was following the counsel of the serpent (against Truth);
the Tzadik and the Bris are the antidote.
The month of Tishray is a complete arc:
Rosh HaShanah (drawing Faith and Truth / beginning of creation);
Ten Days (rectifying through prayer and mitzvos / the 613 counsels);
Yom Kippur (the Second Tablets / completion of Faith);
Sukkos (union of Truth and Faith / Avraham and the Kindnesses);
Sh'mini Atzeres (perfect birth / the Messianic future realized each year anew).

Siman 8 — Roissi Menoras Zohov ["I Saw a Menora of Gold" — Zech. 4]

Theme: The Spirit of Life, Rosh HaShanah, and the Nullification of the Storm-Wind of Esov

On Rosh HaShanah the Renewal of Creation is Drawn — The Spirit of Life

On Rosh HaShanah the dimension of the renewal of creation is drawn —
which came through the dimension of the spirit of life (ruach chaim),
as is explained in the main text.
And then the Books of Life and the Books of Death
are opened before Him —
and the completely righteous — who cleave to the holy Torah,
wherein is the primary spirit of life —
are immediately inscribed for life.
The completely wicked — who are entirely distant from the holiness of the holy Torah —
are therefore immediately inscribed for death —
for they are distant from the holy spirit of life.
Even in their physical lifetimes they are called dead.
The intermediate ones — who have good and evil intermingled —
are therefore suspended until Yom Kippur.

For on Yom Kippur all Israel in general merit to separate and distinguish the evil from the good —
the dimension of:
"one lot for G-d and one lot for Azazel"
[Lev. 16:8]
— for then the holiness of Torah and prayer is drawn in completeness,
through which the evil is separated from the good.
For then Moshe received the Second Tablets —
the essential holy Torah, comprising the Ten Commandments —
from which the ten types of spiritual arousal (minei d'fokin)
that awaken the spirit of life are received.

And likewise prayer is completed most fully at that time —
the dimension of the Five Prayers of Yom Kippur.
And Moshe our Teacher merited to receive the Second Tablets at that time also
only through his many prayers —
and the disclosure of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy
which G-d revealed to him —
all of which is the dimension of drawing the spirit of life through the holy Tzadikim
to complete the lacks and to atone for sins —
the dimension of "a wise man can appease it."

And therefore on Yom Kippur Moshe accomplished the drawing of forgiveness of sins
for eternal generations —
and then the dimension of the rule of Esov —
the man of Seir — the dimension of the spirit of the storm (ruach seara) — was completely subdued.
The dimension of:
"and the he-goat shall carry upon itself all their sins to a desolate land"
[Lev. 16:22]
— the Sages, z"l, expounded this of Esov.

[The forces of accusation] intensify greatly [on Rosh HaShanah]
— and therefore one must not mention any sin or transgression [on Rosh HaShanah itself],
so as not to give them increased strength —
for their primary vitality and the intensification of the storm-wind of [Esov]
derives only from the sins of Israel, heaven forbid.

And therefore the obligation is most intense at that time
to go and journey to the true Tzadik on Rosh HaShanah —
in order to draw through him the dimension of extended breath (arichas ruach)
to complete all the lacks
and to overpower and humble the dimension of the husk of Esov and his princes, heaven forbid,
through the strength of this Tzadik
who is in the dimension of Rav Chesed V'Emes — great in loving-kindness and truth.

This is the dimension of the great war that takes place at that time
between Yaakov and Esov, as brought in the Zohar.
This is the dimension of:
"a day of Teruah shall it be for you"
[Num. 29:1]
— and it is explained in the Zohar that this is the dimension of:
"and when you go to war in your land against the enemy who oppresses you —
and you shall sound the Teruah"
[Num. 10:9].
For all the wars from the distressing oppressor
all come from the dimension of the storm-wind of Esov.
And one must humble it through the voice of the Teruah —
which is the dimension of the holy sigh (anochah),
the dimension of extended breath (arichas ruach) —
to complete the lacks and to overpower the storm-wind of Esov and his princes.

And this is why the Sages, z"l, were uncertain about the Teruah:
whether it is Sh'vorim — which is "groaning-groaning" [gonochi gonach] —
that is, the holy sigh above —
which is the dimension of the extended holy breath,
and through it the storm-wind is subdued;
or whether it is Teruah — which is "wailing-wailing" [yelulai yeilil] —
i.e., short and rapid sounds —
for this corresponds to the storm-wind of Esov
which intensifies with great panic and great speed,
and the troubles that come from it are close and rapid, one after another,
as the Sages, z"l, taught:
"Until the first one takes notice, the second hurries and hastens to come."

Therefore they agreed to do both.
And therefore the Sh'vorim and the Teruah must be done in one breath (neshima),
and some say that also both the Sh'vorim and the Teruah together
must be done in one breath —
for all of this is the dimension of the extended holy breath and respiration.
And in any case, in the Tashra"T sequence
[Tekia-Sh'vorim-Teruah-Tekia]
one must not pause between Sh'vorim and Teruah
[even] for the length of a breath —
for in this sequence, both are performed to demonstrate that both are needed and each depends upon the other.
And Sh'vorim precedes Teruah —
for through the sigh and extended holy breath — which is the dimension of Sh'vorim —
one overpowers the storm-wind of Esov and his princes —
which is alluded to in Teruah, as above.

And this is what the Sages, z"l, taught:
"Teruah alludes to the Torah — the letters Tav-Vav-Reish-Hay"
— for the essential extension of the spirit of life is received from the holy Torah.
And likewise the essential humbling of Esov the man of Seir
is through the holy Torah —
as the Sages, z"l, expounded:
"the voice is the voice of Yaakov"
[Gen. 27:22].

And because the masses of the people cannot receive
the extension of the spirit of life and the completion of their lacks from the holy Torah —
except through the Tzadik and the Torah teacher of the generation —
therefore every Teruah has a simple [Tekia] before it and after it.
For the simple Tekia alludes to the gathering and connecting to the Tzadik —
as is explained in the passage of the trumpets:
"and you shall blow them and all the congregation shall assemble to you"
[Num. 10:3],
as was brought above.

Also, the simple Tekia indicates the completeness that the spirit of life possesses
before a person sins;
and the Teruah indicates the sigh one must sigh over the lack created by the sin —
the dimension of: "there are no sufferings without sin."
But even so, through the sigh one merits to complete the lack —
and this is the dimension of the simple Tekia that follows.
And all of this is through the power of the Tzadik, as above.

And all this entire matter is included in the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy,
as is explained in the main text.
And this is what the Sages, z"l, taught:
"G-d, G-d"
[Ex. 34:6]
— "'G-d' before one sins and 'G-d' after one sins"
— as mentioned above.

And this is the dimension of Malchuyos, Zichronos, and Shofaros:
for the essential holy spirit of life is received from the dimension of holy Malchus
— the dimension of:
"and Esther clothed herself in royalty"
[Esther 5:1]
— and the Sages, z"l, taught that she clothed herself in the holy spirit —
and it is written:
"in the light of the King's countenance is life"
[Prov. 16:15].
And as is understood in the discourse Vayitain Oz L'Malko, Siman 78.
And this is the dimension of:
"and the spirit of G-d hovered over the waters"
— the Sages, z"l, taught: this is the spirit of the King Messiah.

Zichronos — the dimension of completing the lacks and extending the spirit [of life]
that is drawn through the holy sigh —
the dimension of:
"and G-d heard their groaning, and G-d remembered His covenant"
[Ex. 2:24],
and: "and G-d remembered Noach... and G-d caused a wind (ruach) to pass over the earth"
[Gen. 8:1]
— ruach specifically, as above.
And this is the dimension of:
"remember, that my life is wind (ruach)"
[Job 7:7].
And this is the dimension of:
"for there is no mention of You in death"
[Ps. 6:6]
— for death is the opposite of the holy spirit of life,
which is the dimension of remembrance.

And "through what? Through the Shofar" —
i.e., Shofaros,
in which one recalls at length the Giving of the Torah
— from which the primary spirit of life comes —
and one concludes with verses of the Prophets
about how the redemption and the ingathering of the exiles
— the humbling of the storm-wind of Esov the man of Seir —
will be through the Shofar.
And through this, ultimately, the storm-wind will swirl upon them,
as is explained in the main text.
And this is the dimension of:
"And G-d the L-rd shall blow the Shofar and shall go in the storms of the south wind"
[Zech. 9:14]
— meaning: the storm-wind shall be stirred up against them —
and upon us G-d of Hosts shall protect, etc.

Afterwards One Engages in Repentance — Yom Kippur

Afterwards one engages in repentance throughout all the Ten Days of Repentance —
to rectify the blemish of sins
from which the storm-wind draws sustenance —
to clarify and separate the evil from the good within the four elements —
and to strengthen the spirit of life of the Tzadikim
over the storm-wind of the wicked.
And one multiplies holy cries and sighs
until on Yom Kippur one merits forgiveness of sins
and the completion of lacks through the holy spirit of life, as above.
And therefore one stands the entire day wrapped in a tallis and tzitzis,
and recites many times the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy —
all of which is the dimension of drawing the holy spirit of life, as explained in the main text.

After Yom Kippur — Sukkos: The Loving-Kindnesses Illuminate

After Yom Kippur, the light of the loving-kindnesses
begins to enter and to shine —
through which the essential sweetening of judgments
and overpowering of the princes of Esov takes place.
This is the dimension of:
"preserving loving-kindness to thousands"
[Ex. 34:7],
as is explained in the main text.
Until on the first day of Sukkos,
the great inner loving-kindness enters —
and also the supernal encompassing loving-kindness —
which is the dimension of the white tallis
in which G-d arranged the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.

For the tallis is in the dimension of an encompassing [light] (makif),
as is understood in the discourse LaShemesh, Siman 49 —
which is the dimension of the spirit of life —
the dimension of:
"the spirit goes about and returns"
[Eccl. 1:6],
as is explained in the main text.
And therefore one enters the Sukka —
which is the dimension of encompassing lights (oiros hamakifin),
as is explained in the discourse Atika, Siman 21.

Also, the Sukka alludes to Bina —
for there is the primary spirit of life, as explained in the main text.
And from there the life of the King is drawn to the dimension of Malchus
— the dimension of the Sukka of David that has fallen — to raise and support it.
And the essential rectification of Malchus is through loving-kindnesses —
the dimension of "and through kindness a throne is established", as brought above.
And this is the dimension of:
"and life and kindness You have done with me"
[Job 10:12].

(And therefore the Sukka is a remembrance of the Clouds of Glory
that protected Israel from the war of Amaleik —
who is from the princes of Esov —
for the supernal loving-kindness that enters on the first day of Sukkos
is the dimension of "preserving loving-kindness to thousands," as above.)

And this is the dimension of the four species that are taken at that time —
and the Sages, z"l, taught that they all allude to the Holy One, blessed be He.
And in the holy writings it is explained that they correspond to
the four letters of the Name Havaya, blessed be He —
meaning they hint that we have been victorious in the war
through being grasped and cleaved to the holy spirit of life —
which is the dimension of the four letters of Havaya,
the dimension of the spirit of life and the good
within all four elements, as is understood in the main text.

Translator's Summary — Siman 8

Siman 8 frames the entire High Holiday season through the lens of
Ruach Chaim (the Spirit of Life) versus the Ruach Seara (the Storm-Wind of Esov).
The Shofar debate (Sh'vorim vs. Teruah) reflects both strategies for overcoming the storm-wind:
the extended, deep sigh of holy breath (Sh'vorim)
and the rapid, urgent cries that counter Esov's quick-striking attacks (Teruah).
The Tzadik — the embodiment of Ruach Chaim — is the conduit for all rectification.
The Three Blessings map precisely: Malchuyos = holy sovereignty / Esther's spirit; Zichronos = G-d's remembering / holy wind; Shofaros = Torah / the Shofar of final redemption.
After Yom Kippur, the loving-kindnesses of the first day of Sukkos
correspond to the white tallis and the Thirteen Attributes —
the encompassing spirit-of-life that protects and nourishes the Four Species' victory.

Missing Sub-Sections of Siman 8 — Roissi Menoras Zohov

The Four Species — Through the Lens of the Spirit of Life

And this is what the Sages, z"l, expounded: Peri Eitz Hadar — this is Avraham — the dimension of the loving-kindness above. Kapos Smorim — this is Yitzchok — the dimension of the attribute of judgment, from which the storm-wind of the princes of Esov derives its sustenance — but through the loving-kindness of Avraham it too is sweetened, in the secret of the Akaidah of Yitzchok, as is known — the dimension of "preserving loving-kindness to thousands" [Ex. 34:7]. And therefore it is explained in the Kavanos of the blessing of Zichronos: "Just as Avraham our Father suppressed his mercies, etc., so may Your mercies suppress Your anger against us," which is the dimension of "preserving loving-kindness to thousands."

Anaf Eitz Avos — this is Yaakov, corresponding to the dimension of Ruach (spirit), as is known; also the dimension of the Torah from which the spirit of life flows, as above. Arvay Nachal — this is Yosef — the dimension of the Tzadik through whom the spirit of life is received, the dimension of "a man in whom the spirit of G-d dwells" said of Yosef — and from him all receive the holy spirit of life, the dimension of "for G-d sent me to give life… to preserve many people" [Gen. 45:7–8].

And more was expounded: Peri Eitz Hadar — this is Sarah, who is the dimension of the holy Malchus from which the spirit of life is received, as above. Therefore she merited complete good life without lack, as Rashi explains: "all the years of Sarah were equal in goodness" — for she was at the age of one hundred as at the age of twenty in regard to sin, and thus she did not blemish the holy spirit of life at all. Kapos Smorim — this is Rivka, from whom came Yaakov and Esov — the dimension of the sweetening of the storm-wind of Esov the man of Seir through Yaakov, who is the dimension of the holy spirit of life. And therefore Yaakov our Father did not die, as the Sages, z"l, taught. And Esov said: "I am going to die" — the dimension of "the wicked in their lifetimes are called dead" — since they have no holy spirit of life.

For Yaakov was the dimension of the great Rabbi of holiness — Rav Chesed V'Emes — great in loving-kindness and truth — the dimension of "grant truth to Yaakov, loving-kindness to Avraham" [Mic. 7:20]. And therefore when he feared Esov he said: "I am diminished by all the loving-kindnesses and all the truth" [Gen. 32:11] — for the essential humbling of Esov is through the dimension of great loving-kindness and truth.

Anaf Eitz Avos — this is Leah. Arvay Nachal — this is Rachel. Leah is the dimension of alma d'iskasiyan — the hidden world — the dimension of prayer, which is the dimension of "an eye has not seen [You], G-d" [Is. 64:3], as is explained in the main text. Rachel is the dimension of alma d'isgalyan — the revealed world — the dimension of Torah. For through prayer and Torah one merits to clarify and separate the evil from the good, and to cleave to the spirit of life, and to humble the storm-wind above.

And more was expounded: the four species allude to the Sanhedrin, who engage in clarifying the laws of Torah — thereby separating the evil from the good in the four elements. And more was expounded: they allude to the dimension of "all my bones shall say [G-d, who is like You]" — the dimension of the completeness of prayer. For in holiness, each dimension is itself comprised of many dimensions.

And this is: the esrog resembles the heart — wherein is the primary spirit of life. The lulav resembles the spine — which is the dimension of the Tzadik who is the life of the worlds, through whom the spirit of life is drawn to complete all lacks. The hadas resembles the eyes — the dimension of the clarification of the laws of Torah — the dimension of "enlighten our eyes in Your Torah." The arova resembles the lips — the dimension of prayer.

And more was expounded: the four species allude to all the groupings within Israel — the essential point being that they all form one bundle — for this is one of G-d's kindnesses: that He contracted Himself, as it were, so that the spirit of life would be present with the Tzadikim — allowing the Tzadikim to draw the spirit of life to complete the lacks for all who cleave and connect to them, even those who have blemished the holy Torah — and to return them in repentance and atone for their sin.

And this is the dimension of the joy with the four species — "and you shall rejoice before G-d your G-d" [Lev. 23:40] — for since one merits to the completeness of lacks, one is filled with joy. And the primary joy is also from the dimension of the spirit of life — the dimension of "restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and let a generous spirit uphold me" [Ps. 51:14].

Sh'mini Atzeres — The Spirit of Life is Perfected

Afterwards one merits Sh'mini Atzeres — and then the union of the Matron in completeness. And likewise below, the Tzadik unites with all of Knesses Yisroel in complete union, and draws upon them the spirit of life from the holy Torah. Therefore all Israel ascend at that time to the Torah and complete the Torah in the matter of the breaking of the Tablets — accomplished so as not to give the storm-wind an opportunity to draw sustenance, as it were, from the Torah itself — the dimension of "the one who pursues evil — it will come upon him" [Prov. 11:27]. Therefore Moshe descended to the depths of the law, argued by analogy from his own reasoning, and broke the Tablets — and G-d agreed with him. Afterward Moshe prayed greatly until G-d revealed to him the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy — which hint at the secret of how the Tzadik can draw the spirit of life to complete lacks and atone for sins. He thereby merited to receive the Second Tablets, which encompass the entire Torah wherein is the primary spirit of life.

And this is why one immediately begins again with Bereishis bara Elokim — "In the beginning G-d created" — and "the earth was void and formless," etc., which alludes to the intensification of the rule of the four kingdoms through the storm-wind that draws from the evil in the four elements. The rectification is through "and the spirit of G-d hovered over the waters" — the spirit of life resting in the holy Torah. "And G-d said: Let there be light" — "and G-d separated between the light and the darkness" — He separated and distinguished the evil from the good. "Evening" — this is the evening of Esov. "Morning" — this is the morning of Yaakov, for ultimately the holy spirit of life of Yaakov will overpower and nullify the storm-wind of Esov — and then the purpose of creation will be fulfilled and all creation will emerge from potential to actuality. Then we will merit the day that is entirely Shabbos — which is what the Torah portion concludes with. And then the [feminine] retains the drop — which carries the spirit of life — so that it does not miscarry — hinting at the secret of the final redemption after which there will be no further exile, for the storm-wind of impurity is completely humbled. And then the joy is exceedingly great, and Yaakov is the head of joy.

[Appendix to the Above]

[Appended note:] And this is what the Sages, z"l, taught: in merit of "take for yourselves on the first day" — "I will reveal Myself to you as the First" — for in merit of the four species, which show that we are bound and cleaved to the holy spirit of life which is the dimension of the soul — and currently the soul itself is not visible and revealed, certainly G-d Who is the source of the spirit of life — "for with You is the source of life" — He certainly sees but is not seen. But in the future, when the four elements are refined to become the dimension of the four letters of Havaya, "the glory of G-d will be revealed." "And He pays back to you from the First — this is Esov" — the nullification of the storm-wind of Esov. "And He builds for you the First — this is the Temple" — wherein is the primary place of prayer, the clarification of the laws of Torah, and the Sanhedrin. "And He brings for you the First — this is King Messiah" — who is the primary spirit of life of all Israel.

Translator's Summary — Siman 8 (Completed)
The three missing sub-sections of Siman 8 complete the picture of Ruach Chaim vs. Ruach Seara: the Four Species map the Patriarchs and Matriarchs to the spirit of life — Yosef drawing it from G-d directly; Sarah receiving it through Malchus; Yaakov as the Tzadik who never dies; Rachel and Leah as prayer and Torah. The appended note ties together: the four species = the four letters of Havaya = the fully refined spirit of life. Sh'mini Atzeres = the Tzadik's perfect union with all of Israel, drawing the spirit of life through Torah, completing the rectification begun on Erev Rosh HaShanah at the Tzadik's grave.

Siman 9 — Sihomoas Yichas'yoomoo ["The depths covered them" — Ex. 15:5]
Theme: Prayer, Truth, and the Rectification of the Day of Judgment

See Likutay Halachos — And Further Elaboration

See Likutay Halachos, Laws of Rosh HaShanah, Law 1, where the entire topic of Rosh HaShanah through this discourse is explained. And to elaborate somewhat further:

On Rosh HaShanah we are engaged in building the holy Malchus, which stands upon twelve oxen, as is explained elsewhere. This is the dimension of prayer — which is the dimension of Malchus, and has twelve texts (nuscha'os), and ascends through twelve gates. And because the primary vitality is received through prayer, and likewise the primary sustenance flows from there — therefore one prays extensively at that time: "Remember us for life" and "inscribe us in the Book of Life." And the Sages, z"l, taught: "a person's sustenance is apportioned to him from Rosh HaShanah."

And this is the dimension of what we engage in from Rosh HaShanah to Sh'mini Atzeres: to complete the dimension of the union of the Matron (zivuga d'Matronissa) — which depends primarily upon prayer, as is explained in the main text.

And this is the dimension of the Day of Judgment on Rosh HaShanah — for the essential judgment upon a person is for not having been careful in the matter of prayer. For through prayer one can come to all goodness: to Torah, to good deeds, to repentance, and to escape from sin — as the Sages, z"l, established many prayers for this. And this is understood from the words of the Sages, z"l (Eruvin 65a), where Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah said: "I can exempt the entire world from judgment," etc. And the conclusion is: from what judgment? — from the judgment of prayer. For the judgment of prayer is the total accounting of a person — for had he been careful and diligent in prayer as is fitting, he would have merited to rectify everything. And this is also explained in the commentators in a similar vein, and as is explained by us elsewhere — for this is learned from the matter of the betrothed maiden, whose primary liability to death, heaven forbid, is for the fact that "she did not cry out" [Deut. 22:24], etc.

But when a person stands to pray, the darkness and the husks surround him from all sides and confuse his prayer — this is the dimension of the alien thoughts (machshavos zaros) in prayer. Therefore the essential rectification of prayer is through truth (emes) — for through truth G-d dwells with him — and when G-d is with him, He illuminates for him how to emerge from the darkness, as it is written: "G-d is my light" [Ps. 27:1] — see there. And this is the dimension of the great accusations that intensify on Rosh HaShanah — and G-d in His mercy illuminates us with the dimension of "G-d is my light," as the Sages, z"l, expounded. And therefore He commanded us to hear the voice of the Shofar — and through this the judgment and the darkness are sweetened, by arousing the quality of Yaakov, as is explained in the holy Zohar — the dimension of "a day of Teruah shall it be for you." And the quality of Yaakov is truth — as it is written: "grant truth to Yaakov" [Mic. 7:20] — as is also explained in the abovementioned Likutay Halachos.

Because There Are Two Dimensions of Truth

Because there are two dimensions of truth: there is truth that illuminates of itself — like a precious stone; and there is truth that is only in the dimension of a window — having no light of its own, but through which one can at least draw in the light that shines from outside.

And this is the dimension of what the Sages, z"l, were uncertain about: whether the Teruah is gonochi gonach — the dimension of an ill person who groans and sighs over his illness as long as it has not yet severely burdened him — this being the dimension of truth that is only in the dimension of a window, having no self-illuminating light, for he is still far from the essence of truth, and therefore does not yet feel the full weight of his illness — but even so, he draws himself with his whole heart toward truth, and therefore groans and moans over his great pain. And through this, someone else can at least illuminate within him the illumination of truth, until he can emerge from the darkness. And this is the dimension of Sh'vorim.

Or: the Teruah is yelulai yelil — meaning he truly feels the full weight of his illness pressing upon him, and therefore cries out in truth from the depths of his heart — rapid wailing calls one after the other — the dimension of truth that illuminates of itself like a precious stone.

And therefore the Sages, z"l, established to sound both — and also to sound both together. And first Sh'vorim, then Teruah — for this is the natural sequence with the ill as well. For this is the path: in the beginning one must draw oneself at least toward truth, and incline one's ear, and listen well in one's heart to the holy voice of truth in the words of prayer, and say the words in truth and wholesome simplicity (tmimus) according to one's level, at the very least — for all of this is included in the dimension of "to hear the voice of the Shofar" — the voice of Yaakov, the dimension of truth. And through this itself one merits afterward to come to the light of truth in its essence.

And this is the dimension of the simple Tekia before and after — for Teruah and Sh'vorim are the dimension of drawing the light of truth even when the darkness and husks surround one from all sides — through which one sees the openings for emerging from the darkness, the dimension of "and when you go to war in your land against the enemy who oppresses you — you shall sound the Teruah" [Num. 10:9]. And the simple Tekia indicates the light of holiness and truth itself when the darkness does not surround one. Therefore first one sounds a Tekia, then one sounds the Teruah and merits thereby to emerge from the darkness — and then one sounds the simple Tekia after, so that one merits to enter the holiness of prayer in its completeness.

Also: Teruah alludes to the Torah, as the Sages, z"l, taught — for the rectification of prayer also requires Torah study, as is explained in the main text. And the simple Tekia alludes to the drawing-near to the Tzadik — who is the dimension of Moshe-Messiah, as is explained in the passage of the trumpets, and as is explained above — and to him one must connect all prayers, as is explained in the main text. And because on Rosh HaShanah one is engaged most intensively in the rectification of prayer — therefore then the obligation is greatest to come to the true Tzadik of the highest stature, who is himself comprised of all the prayers, as is explained in the main text.

The Dimension of Malchuyos, Zichronos, and Shofaros

Malchuyos — the dimension of building prayer, which is the dimension of faith (emuna), the dimension of Malchus. Zichronos — the dimension of the completeness of the rectifications of prayer through the light of truth — for through truth [the person] calls G-d to mind within himself in truth, and [G-d] knows all his thoughts and schemes — and therefore his thought is compelled to direct his heart toward Him in truth, according to his level at the very least. Through this, his remembrance ascends before Him for good, and he draws near to Him, and He illuminates for him how to emerge from the darkness and draw near to Him in truth.

And this is the dimension of what Yona said from within the belly of the fish: "You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas" [Jonah 2:4], and "all Your breakers and waves passed over me," etc. (For all of this, and more, a person must say to himself at the time when the darkness and husks and alien thoughts — called "the depths of the sea" — disturb and confuse his thought greatly, and he cannot direct his heart in his prayer.) And he concluded: "when my soul fainted within me, I remembered G-d — and my prayer came before You, into Your holy Temple" [Jonah 2:8], etc.

And this is also the entire matter of the blessing Ata Zocher ["You Remember"] — where it is explained clearly how G-d remembers everything, knows everything, supervises and sets His eyes and heart upon all creatures, and there is no forgetfulness before the Throne of His Glory. And it mentions there the verses of Noach — how G-d remembered him when he sheltered in the Ark. (For there is hinted the matter of how when the floodwaters — which are the dimension of alien thoughts — intensify, one must enter the Ark — meaning: draw all one's strength and focus into the teivos [words/letters] of the words of prayer, the dimension of "come, you and all your household, into the Ark" [Gen. 7:1] as is brought — and to say the word in truth — which is the dimension of "make a window for the Ark," as is explained in the main text.) "And G-d caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided" [Gen. 8:1].

And there are also mentioned other verses of Zichronos — showing how when Israel draw themselves toward truth and cry out to Him, even though they are not yet at the level of the finest self-luminous truth — even so, G-d has mercy upon them and remembers for them the true truth that the Patriarchs merited, and in their merit He illuminates for them and answers them in their time of distress. And one concludes with prayer to recall for us the Akaidah of Yitzchok — through which the judgment and darkness are sweetened at their supernal root. Even though Esov came from Yitzchok and wishes to intensify with his many accusations, etc., as is explained in the holy Zohar — and this itself is also the dimension of the alien thoughts and confusions, for he descends and entices, etc. — even so, he is not counted as part of the seed of Yitzchok at all — for "in Yitzchok shall your seed be called" — and not all [who come from] Yitzchok. And all of this G-d will remember for us now as well, and will illuminate for us His light, and will remove from us all types of darkness and disturbing thoughts, and will sweeten from upon us all the judgments, etc.

Shofaros — there it explains the matter of the Giving of the Torah with the Shofar-sound, and the matter of the Shofar of the Messiah and the ingathering of the exiles — for the rectification of prayer requires also Torah study, as above. And one must also connect prayer to the Tzadik of the generation who is the dimension of the Messiah. And through the completeness of prayer — which is the dimension of miracles, faith, and the Land of Israel — through this one exits the exiles. Therefore one concludes the blessing with prayer for the ingathering of exiles to our Land.

Afterwards — the Ten Days of Repentance

Afterwards one engages in this throughout all the Ten Days of Repentance — for this is the essential repentance: to greatly multiply prayers and supplications before G-d, and to fulfill the scriptural verse: "Arise, cry out in the night… pour out your heart like water" [Lam. 2:19] — which is the dimension of rising at the dawn watch and multiplying supplications before G-d — until one merits the holiness of Yom Kippur. Then prayer is complete, and one prays Five Prayers, and Malchus is nourished from the five innermost voices — the dimension of the very essence of truth — the dimension of "and one who speaks truth in his heart" [Ps. 15:2].

And then the clouds — which are the alien thoughts that come from sins and impede the intention of prayer — [are annulled]. Because of this [on Rosh HaShanah itself] no sin or transgression is mentioned (except during the Shofar-soundings), so as not to intensify the clouds and accusations. But on Yom Kippur "the Accuser has no authority to prosecute" [Yoma 20a], and one merits forgiveness of sins and the nullification of the clouds — the dimension of "I have blotted out as a thick cloud your transgressions, and as a cloud your sins" [Is. 44:22]. Then came the completion of the reception of the Second Tablets — through which the rectifications of prayer were completed. And the service was performed by the High Priest — who is the dimension of the Tzadik of the generation to whom all prayers must be connected. And the High Priest entered at that time into the innermost sanctuary (lifnai v'lifnim) — where is the source of the holiness of the Land of Israel, the source of prayer and miracles. And therefore many miracles were performed then, as brought above in the discourse of Mishpatim, Siman 7.

After Yom Kippur — The Loving-Kindnesses Enter

After Yom Kippur the lights of the loving-kindnesses begin to enter — for through them is the essential rectification of Malchus, as it is written: "and through kindness a throne is established." And as it applies to us: the essential rectification of prayer — which is the dimension of faith — is through the loving-kindnesses, the dimension of "blessed is G-d Who has not removed my prayer and His loving-kindness from me" [Ps. 66:20]. And this is the dimension of "He remembered His loving-kindness and His faithfulness to the house of Israel" [Ps. 98:3]. And likewise: "to declare Your loving-kindness in the morning and Your faithfulness in the nights" [Ps. 92:3]. And also: to the light of truth one merits only through G-d's loving-kindness — the dimension of "grant truth to Yaakov, loving-kindness to Avraham," as is also brought above.

Until on the first day of Sukkos the supernal loving-kindness of the encompassing lights enters too — and then faith — which is also in the dimension of the encompassing lights — is completed in its fullness: the dimension of "Your faithfulness surrounds You" [Ps. 89:9]. And one enters the Sukka — which is also in the dimension of encompassing lights — the dimension of "Sukkos surrounds me" [Ps. 27:5], as is brought in the discourse Atika, Siman 21. And then the Sukka of David is raised up — which is the dimension of complete prayer — by drawing the light of truth from its root: the dimension of the Supernal Sukka, the dimension of Supernal Bina. And then the Blessed Holy One and the Divine Presence are united — for the letters of סוכה spell out Kuf-Vav = 26 and Hay-Samech = 65 [the numerical values of the Names Havaya and Adnay] — for their essential unity is through the completeness of prayer, as is explained in the main text. Also: when the light of truth — which is G-d's light, the very essence of truth — shines upon prayer, which is the dimension of faith and Malchus — this itself is also the unity of the Blessed Holy One and the Divine Presence — the dimension of Sukka, as above. And therefore it is required that stars be visible through the s'chach. Also: סוכה has the same numerical value as מלאך (malach — angel), as is brought also in Likutay Mohara"n Tinyona, Siman 5 — for through complete prayer one conveys strength and vitality even to the world of the stars and the world of the angels.

The Four Species

And this is the dimension of the taking of the four species. The Sages, z"l, expounded: Peri Eitz Hadar — this is Avraham — the dimension of prayer, for he was the first to establish the Morning Prayer (Shacharis), and it is said of him: "and Avraham prayed to G-d" [Gen. 20:17], etc. Kapos Smorim — this is Yitzchok — the dimension of Torah, as the Sages, z"l, taught: "Torah was given from the power of Gevura," as is brought. Anaf Eitz Avos — this is Yaakov — etc. — the dimension of truth above, as it is written: "grant truth to Yaakov." Arvay Nachal — this is Yosef — etc. — the dimension of the Tzadik — for all these dimensions are rectifications of prayer, as above.

Peri Eitz Hadar — this is Sarah — the dimension of prayer, the dimension of Malchus. Kapos Smorim — this is Rivka — from whom came Yaakov and Esov — the dimension of the intensification of alien thoughts during prayer, which come from the side of Esov — the dimension of "for he had [Esov's] game in his mouth" [Gen. 25:28], as is explained in the main text. And the rectification is through Yaakov, who is the dimension of truth, as above. Anaf Eitz Avos — this is Leah — etc. — from whom the Messiah descended, who is comprised of all the prayers. And therefore the hadas (myrtle) has fragrance — for the Messiah "smells and judges", as is explained in the main text. Arvay Nachal — this is Rachel — etc. — who is the dimension of Torah — "like a ewe before her shearers": all shear laws (halachos) from her, etc. — as is explained in the discourse Tehila l'Dovid, Siman 12.

And more was expounded: the four species correspond to the Sanhedrin — whose essential work is Torah. And more was expounded: they correspond to the dimension of "all my bones shall say" — the dimension of the completeness of prayer with all the [bodily] forces, as is explained in the main text.

And this is: the esrog resembles the heart — the dimension of having to direct one's heart in prayer, as it is written: "prepare their heart — incline Your ear" [Ps. 10:17], as the Sages, z"l, expounded — and this is the dimension of "pour out your heart like water," as is explained in the main text. The lulav resembles the spine — for it is the essential connecting structure of the entire frame of the body — meaning: one must pray with all the forces of the body and the movements of all the limbs, the dimension of "all my bones shall say," etc. — to the extent that all the vertebrae of the spine articulate, as the Sages, z"l, taught of Rabbi Akiva: when he prayed privately he would bow deeply many times, etc. The hadas resembles the eyes — for one must say the words of prayer in truth — and through this G-d supervises one with an open eye (eina p'kicha), the dimension of "my eyes are upon the faithful of the land" [Ps. 101:6], etc. — as is also explained in the discourse Amar Rabbi Akiva, Siman 51 — and then He is near to one and illuminates one's eyes on how to emerge from the darkness surrounding one. The arova resembles the lips — the dimension of the words of prayer themselves, the dimension of "G-d, open my lips" [Ps. 51:17]. And therefore one waves them during "Give thanks to G-d" and during "Please, G-d, save now" — for this is the entirety of prayer: thanking for the past and crying out for the future, as the Sages, z"l, said.

And this is the dimension of the joy of Sukkos — for through the completeness of prayer one merits joy, the dimension of "and I will gladden them in My house of prayer" [Is. 56:7], as is also explained in the discourse Chosom B'Soch Chosom,
